Materials and Methods: This pilot study of eight healthy adults examined the effects of sensory information from a video of an activity of daily living on MI under four conditions: no information, auditory information, visual information, and combined auditory and visual information. The MI task involved cutting paper with scissors. Corticospinal excitability during MI was assessed using motor-evoked potentials elicited by transcranial magnetic stimulation, and subjective MI vividness was evaluated using a visual analog scale. Results: Corticospinal excitability differed significantly across the four conditions (no information, auditory information, visual information, and combined auditory and visual information); however, post hoc analyses did not reveal significant differences between individual conditions. In contrast, subjective MI vividness differed significantly across conditions, with the combined auditory and visual condition yielding the highest vividness ratings. Visual information tended to facilitate MI more effectively than auditory information. Conclusions: These findings suggest that combining visual and auditory sensory information enhances the subjective vividness of MI during mental practice for activities of daily living. Incorporating task-related sensory information may therefore support more effective implementation of mental practice in rehabilitation, particularly in occupational therapy practice.

titre: Réutilisation des données de la HAS : rappel du cadre applicable
resume:
Les données publiées par la HAS peuvent être librement utilisées, à condition d’indiquer leur source et leur date de mise à jour.
     En revanche, la HAS ne valide pas les analyses ou les classements réalisés par d’autres organismes.
     Ces organismes sont responsables de leurs méthodes et de leurs résultats.
     La HAS recommande donc de rester prudent et de consulter ses publications officielles sur Qualiscope.

titre: Séniors, femmes enceintes, professionnels en Ehpad : où en est leur vaccination en France en 2025 ?
resume: Santé publique France publie les données de couverture vaccinales chez les adultes en 2025 et rappelle l’importance de s’informer sur la vaccination aux différents âges et périodes de la vie pour se protéger contre les maladies infectieuses.

titre: Grandir avec les écrans. Le dossier de La Santé en action n°474 de juillet-septembre 2026.
resume: Santé publique France publie, dans une nouvelle édition de sa revue La Santé en action, un dossier sur les écrans, un enjeu de santé publique, au regard des effets sur la santé causés par leur omniprésence dans la vie quotidienne des enfants et adolescents.

titre: SIBCA 2026 : le réseau UrBaCS présente ses solutions pour des villes et des bâtiments qui protègent mieux la population de la chaleur
resume: Pour la première fois, les membres fondateurs du réseau Urbanisme, Bâtiment, Chaleur et Santé (UrBaCS) - Santé publique France, le CSTB, l’Ademe et l’EHESP - se sont réunis le 1er septembre 2026 au Salon de l’Immobilier Bas Carbone (SIBCA) afin de présenter les enjeux du réseau, ses objectifs et mobiliser de nouveaux acteurs autour d’une cause urgente : construire des environnements urbains et bâtis qui protègent mieux les populations de la chaleur.

titre: Activité physique et lutte contre la sédentarité : comment Santé publique France accompagne les français ?
resume: A l’occasion de Septembre Bouge, Santé publique France fait le point sur plusieurs moyens d’agir pour lever les freins à la pratique d’activité physique et lutter contre la sédentarité pour améliorer la santé de tous : outils d’auto-évaluation, accompagnement des jeunes et déploiement de projets concrets sur le terrain.

titre: Arboviroses en 2026 : les maladies transmises par les moustiques continuent leur progression cet été
resume: Dans le cadre de la surveillance renforcée en France hexagonale, Santé publique France publie chaque semaine un point de situation sur les arboviroses et rappelle l’importance des gestes à adopter pour se protéger des piqûres de moustiques.

titre: Hantavirus Andes : mise en place des investigations épidémiologiques et du contact tracing suite à la détection d’un cas importé sur le territoire
resume: Les autorités sanitaires ont été informées d’un cas d’hantavirus Andes ayant transité sur le territoire. La souche Andes a été confirmée par le CNR ce jeudi 6 août. Le patient, isolé avec sa famille en Espagne, est une personne en voyage touristique qui a transité en France la deuxième quinzaine du mois de juillet. Le patient a présenté peu de symptômes et est guéri à ce jour. Des investigations épidémiologiques ont immédiatement été engagées afin de reconstituer son parcours sur le territoire français et d’identifier les personnes-contacts à risque (contrat-tracing)

titre: Voyage en Outre-mer et à l’étranger : êtes-vous à jour de vos vaccins ?
resume: La période estivale est propice aux séjours en outre-mer ou à l’étranger. А̀ cette occasion, Santé publique France rappelle l’importance de vérifier et de mettre à jour ses vaccinations avant de voyager.

titre: Rencontres de Santé publique France : 9 novembre 2026
resume: Les Rencontres de Santé publique France se tiendront le 9 novembre prochain au Beffroi de Montrouge. Cette 9e édition rassemblera la communauté scientifique, les décideurs, la société civile, les acteurs du réseau national de santé publique et des experts français, européens et internationaux. L’occasion de partager leurs expériences en matière de veille sanitaire, d’actions de prévention et d’intervention en santé autour du fil rouge de l’innovation.Cet événement scientifique se clôturera par la remise des prix aux lauréats de la 1ère édition de « l’Odissé Dataviz Challenge : par Santé publique France ». Elle sera suivie d’une journée de formation inédite animée par les experts de l’agence le 10 novembre.

titre: Santé publique France publie son Rapport annuel 2025 : 10 ans d’engagement pour la santé de tous
resume: A l’occasion de ses 10 ans, Santé publique France publie son rapport annuel 2025 accompagné d’un film et d’une infographie pour illustrer une décennie d’actions, d’expertises et de résultats concrets au service de la santé publique.

titre: Point de situation sur la mortalité toutes causes confondues  sur la période du 22 au 28 juin 2026
resume: Les données de surveillance sanitaire de la mortalité toutes causes confondues pour la semaine du 22 au 28 juin 2026 montrent une augmentation de près de 30% des décès toutes causes par rapport à la semaine précédente.

titre: Alcoomètre : bilan après 6 années d’utilisation par les Français pour évaluer leur consommation d’alcool
resume: Accessible sur le site Alcool-info-service.fr, l’alcoomètre permet aux utilisateurs d’évaluer leur consommation d’alcool et d’obtenir un bilan personnalisé. Santé publique France a publié une analyse de 6 années d’utilisation de ce dispositif d’autoévaluation.

titre: G7 à Evian : une surveillance sanitaire renforcée
resume: Dans le cadre de la présidence du G7 qui se déroule du 15 au 17 juin 2026 à Evian (Haute-Savoie), la cellule régionale Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes de Santé publique France est mobilisée afin d’apporter son appui et son expertise à la mise en place d’un dispositif de veille et de surveillance adapté à ce type d’événement.

titre: « Protéger la population des risques de l’alcool ». Le dossier de La Santé en action n°473 d’avril-juin 2026
resume: Santé publique France publie, dans une nouvelle édition de sa revue La Santé en action, un dossier sur l’alcool, un enjeu de santé publique, au regard des dégâts sanitaires et sociaux causés par sa consommation.

titre: Appel à candidature pour compléter le Comité national des infections associées aux soins, de la résistance aux antibiotiques et du bon usage des antibiotiques (CominaPIA)
resume: Santé publique France lance un appel à candidature dans le cadre d'un remplacement de l'un des membres experts du comité. Date limite de candidatures : 30/09/2026.

titre: Semaine de la santé sexuelle 2026 : le dépistage et la prévention restent essentiels
resume: Santé publique France rediffuse sa campagne digitale « Tout le monde se pose des questions sur la sexualité et tout le monde peut trouver des réponses sur QuestionSexualite.fr » du 1er au 28 juin 2026. L’agence rappelle l’importance de s’informer et de dialoguer pour prévenir les situations pouvant nuire à sa santé sexuelle.

titre: 10 ans d'engagement et d'action au service de la santé publique
resume: En dix ans, les enjeux de santé publique se sont intensifiés : multiplication des crises sanitaires, dérèglement climatique, accroissement des inégalités de santé sociales et territoriales, vieillissement de la population. Face à ces mutations, Santé publique France a su s'adapter, innover et agir. Retour sur une décennie d'actions.

titre: Prolongation de l’appel à candidatures pour le renouvellement du comité de rédaction du Bulletin épidémiologique hebdomadaire (BEH)
resume: Santé publique France lance un appel à candidatures pour le renouvellement du comité de rédaction du BEH. La date limite de candidatures est repoussée au 15 septembre 2026.

titre: Lancement du réseau « chaleur-santé-bâti-urbanisme » : vers des villes et des bâtiments résilients face aux canicules
resume: Face à l’intensification des vagues de chaleur et à leurs impacts sanitaires de plus en plus lourds, Santé publique France et ses partenaires ont lancé officiellement le réseau Chaleur-Santé-Bâti-urbanisme (UrBaCS). Ce réseau inédit vise à faire évoluer les pratiques professionnelles des maîtres d’œuvre et maîtres d’ouvrage impliqués dans les projets d’aménagement, de construction et de rénovation, afin de définir des projets résilients aux fortes chaleurs.

titre: La pollution de l’air : des progrès pour notre santé nécessaires et possibles
resume: A l’occasion de la Journée nationale de la qualité de l’air du 14 octobre 2025, Santé publique France publie une infographie sur l’intérêt des actions qui permettent d’améliorer la qualité de l’air et les bénéfices directs sur notre santé.

titre: Journée mondiale de lutte contre le sida 2025 : promouvoir la prévention pour lutter contre la transmission du VIH et des IST
resume: A l’occasion de la Journée mondiale de lutte contre le sida, Santé publique France fait le point sur les données de surveillance du VIH et des IST en France en 2024 et rappelle que le dépistage reste le meilleur moyen pour s’en protéger.

titre: Enquêtes EpiCOV et Sapris : quels sont les enjeux biologiques ?
resume: Santé publique France apporte son expertise dans l’organisation du volet biologique des enquêtes EpiCOV et Sapris afin de connaître le statut immunitaire de la population française et répond aux questions sur les enjeux de ce volet biologique

titre: Odissé : le nouveau portail open data de Santé publique France au service de tous
resume: Santé publique France met à disposition un large éventail d’indicateurs de santé construits grâce à plus de 70 systèmes de surveillance qu’elle pilote et anime, aux enquêtes qu’elle réalise et à son expertise scientifique. Tous les indicateurs produits sont accessibles et disponibles sous Odissé, le nouveau portail open data de l’agence.

titre: Appel à candidatures complémentaire pour la surveillance nationale des expositions des patients atteints de mésothéliome pleural en inter région nord
resume: Santé publique France lance un appel à candidatures complémentaire en vue de sélectionner le CRPPE « référent interrégional » Nord pour réaliser la mission de surveillance des conditions d'exposition des patients atteints de mésothéliomes pleuraux. Date limite : 30 janvier 2026 à 12H00.

titre: Appel à projet pour les missions nationales de surveillance et de prévention des infections associées aux soins et de l’antibiorésistance (mandature 01/10/23 – 30/09/28)
resume: Santé publique France lance un appel à projet pour le renouvellement des missions nationales concernant la prévention des infections associées aux soins augmentées d’un volet relatif au bon usage des antibiotiques. Retrouvez toutes les modalités pour déposer un dossier.

titre: La position sociale : une notion clé pour comprendre et agir sur les inégalités de santé
resume: Santé publique France publie une synthèse méthodologique sur l’impact de la position sociale et son rôle dans la prise en compte des inégalités sociales de santé en s’appuyant sur des outils concrets et des modèles conceptuels robustes.

titre: Port du masque, lavage des mains et aération des pièces : cet hiver, retrouvons le réflexe des gestes barrières
resume: Santé publique France, en lien avec le Ministère chargé de la santé et l’Assurance maladie, rappellent l’importance de l’adoption des gestes barrières pour limiter les épidémies hivernales, dans une nouvelle campagne de prévention diffusée depuis le 25 octobre 2025.

titre: Enquête « Rapport au sexe » (ERAS) 2026 à destination des hommes ayant des rapports sexuels avec des hommes
resume: Santé publique France, en partenariat avec l’ANRS - Maladies infectieuses émergentes, lance la 5e édition de l’enquête Santé Sexualité-Prévention « Rapport au sexe », du 16 mars au 26 avril 2026, à destination des hommes ayant des rapports sexuels avec des hommes.

titre: Grandes causes de décès en France : tendances et causes associées en 2024
resume: La Direction de la recherche, des études, de l’évaluation et des statistiques (Drees), l’Inserm via son Centre d’épidémiologie sur les causes médicales de décès (CépiDc- Inserm) et Santé publique France analysent les causes médicales de décès des personnes résidentes et décédées en France en 2024. Trois études complémentaires sont publiées conjointement : un Bulletin épidémiologique hebdomadaire (Santé publique France) et deux Études et Résultats (Drees). Elles s’appuient sur la statistique nationale des causes de décès produite par l’Inserm (CépiDc) à partir du recueil exhaustif des volets médicaux des certificats de décès, de leur codage et de leur analyse.

titre: Semaine européenne de la vaccination 2026 : protéger dès le plus jeune âge et mieux vacciner les adolescents en Provence-Alpes-Côte d’Azur
resume: La Semaine européenne de la vaccination (SEV), organisée au niveau national par le Ministère de la Santé, des Familles, de l’Autonomie et des Personnes handicapées et Santé publique France se déroule cette année du 27 avril au 3 mai. En 2026, elle met particulièrement l’accent sur la vaccination des adolescents et des jeunes adultes. L’objectif : mieux protéger ces populations en renforçant la promotion des vaccinations contre les infections à papillomavirus humains (HPV) et les méningocoques, dont les recommandations vaccinales ont récemment évolué.

titre: Artificial intelligence integration in allied health professions: A comprehensive review of educational, research, and clinical applications.
auteurs: DeOliveira Shushawna, Rappaport Suzanne, Struk Iryna, Yannotta Richard, Haeri Farhad, Dhaliwal Puneet, Trimmingham Andrea, Hinds Lynette, Amar-Alattaby Amal, Wiggins Shakima, Lewis Allen, Kaufman David, Jumbo Adiebonye, Faysel Mohammad
resume: BackgroundArtificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming healthcare delivery across multiple disciplines. Allied health professions-including diagnostic medical sonography (DMS), health informatics (HI), medical billing and coding (MBC), midwifery (MW), occupational therapy (OT), physical therapy (PT), and physician assistant (PA) practice-represent critical yet understudied domains of AI integration. Understanding of how AI technologies are adopted across these professions is essential for supporting ethical and effective implementation.ObjectiveThis review synthesizes the current literature on AI integration across seven allied health professions, examining applications in education, research, and clinical practice while identifying implementation challenges, and ethical considerations.MethodsA structured literature review of peer-reviewed articles, systematic reviews, and professional practice guidelines published between 2018 and 2025 was conducted. Articles were selected based on relevance to AI applications in allied health professions and discussion of educational, research, or clinical implementations. Particular attention was given to applications where AI augments rather than replaces clinical judgment and therapeutic relationships.ResultsAI integration demonstrates several cross-disciplinary trends. In education, simulation platforms, adaptive learning systems, and virtual patient support competency development and personalized instruction. In research, AI enhances large-scale data analysis, predictive modeling, and evidence synthesis. Clinically, AI improves diagnostic accuracy, workflow efficiency, and decision support across professions. However, implementation raises concerns regarding data privacy, algorithmic bias, automation complacency, and inequitable access to technology.ConclusionsAI is reshaping allied health education, research, and clinical practice. Responsible integration requires discipline-specific validation, ethical governance, and interprofessional collaboration to ensure AI strengthens- rather than replaces-professional expertise and patient-centered care.

titre: Lifestyle Documentation in Therapy Evaluations for Autistic Children: A Lexicon-Based Analysis of Electronic Health Records.
auteurs: Dallman Aaron R, Santucci Gregory, Lai Diana, Welch Caroline, Jimenez Manuel E
revue: The American journal of occupational therapy : official publication of the American Occupational Therapy Association
resume: BackgroundWhole person health (WPH) is a multidimensional construct encompassing, physical, and mental health along with relational constructs such as social health that are deeply tied to well-being. Autistic individuals report an overall lower quality of life, but the extent to which these issues are addressed during therapy evaluations has not been examined systematically.MethodologyIn this retrospective, cross-sectional study, we employ a rule-based NLP/lexicon-based approach to examine the areas of focus of therapy evaluations documented by occupational therapy, physical therapy (PT), and speech-language pathology (SLP) professionals. Using electronic health records for children aged 2 to 18 diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) (n = 5619 evaluation reports of n = 2021 unique patients), we classified health records based on the domains addressed.ResultsAcross notes, nutrition had the highest average degree of documentation (M = 2.14), compared to activity (M = 0.91), followed by wellness (M = 0.66), and sleep (M = 0.39). In occupational therapy, wellness was the most common (77.62% of notes), followed by physical activity (76.49% of notes), nutrition management (73.33% of notes), and sleep (34.97% of notes). The overall area under the curve (AUC) from the receiver operating characteristic analysis is 0.89.ConclusionsWhile it is encouraging that most evaluations addressed nutrition or physical activity, the near absence of attention to sleep represents a critical gap in care. Given sleep's foundational role in overall health and daily functioning, its omission is particularly concerning. Occupational therapists and interdisciplinary rehabilitation teams should more deliberately integrate WPH frameworks into their evaluations.
type_etude: Étude observationnelle (détection par mots-clés, à confirmer)

titre: Art Analysis in Occupational Therapy Education: Building Foundational Skills and Reflective Awareness of Implicit Bias.
auteurs: Lockhart-Keene LaRonda, Persia Susan M
resume: Occupational therapy education requires instructional approaches that help students move beyond memorizing foundational concepts to applying them in meaningful ways. This instructional insight describes the integration of structured art analysis into a first-semester Occupational Competence course as an experiential strategy for teaching the Occupational Therapy Practice Framework (OTPF-4) and activity analysis. Through individual, classroom, and museum-based learning experiences, students engaged in guided observation, discussion, reflection, and application using artwork as a low-risk context for developing observational and interpretive skills. Evidence of student learning included confidence surveys and written reflections completed throughout the instructional sequence. Students reported increased confidence in applying OTPF concepts and activity analysis, while reflections demonstrated greater awareness of how personal experiences and implicit bias can influence interpretation. Students also described the importance of considering multiple perspectives and avoiding premature assumptions before drawing conclusions. By intentionally connecting art analysis to occupational therapy practice, this instructional approach helped students apply foundational occupational therapy concepts while fostering reflective awareness that supports thoughtful professional judgment. Structured art analysis offers occupational therapy educators an engaging and adaptable strategy for promoting active learning and preparing students to apply foundational knowledge in future clinical practice.

titre: Sarcopenia and cognitive impairment after hip fracture in older adults: a narrative review and conceptual rehabilitation framework.
auteurs: Han Qi, Bai Hong-Zhao
resume: Hip fracture in later life is followed by high mortality, incomplete recovery of mobility, and frequent loss of independence. Sarcopenia and cognitive impairment are common at presentation yet are often assessed and treated as separate determinants of recovery. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on their joint clinical impact, plausible links, and rehabilitation implications. In a 2025 rehabilitation cohort, independent ambulation was recovered by 60.8% of participants with both conditions versus 90.2% with neither; the combined phenotype was associated with a 57% lower likelihood of walking recovery. Recent studies also associate sarcopenia with postoperative delirium and early postoperative cognitive decline, whereas cognitive impairment is linked to more complications, less rehabilitation referral, and poorer function. Mechanistic translation remains incomplete: the FNDC5/irisin-BDNF axis has not been shown to mediate recovery in hip-fracture cohorts because target engagement, biomarker source, assay comparability, and perioperative confounding remain unresolved. We therefore propose an evidence-informed, phase-specific conceptual framework incorporating orthogeriatric assessment, delirium prevention, progressive resistance and task-specific exercise, individualized protein-energy support, cognitively adapted communication and motor learning, management of concerns about falling, and supported continuity after discharge. The framework integrates components supported by hip-fracture studies with recommendations extrapolated from broader geriatric guidance; it has not been validated as a complete care pathway for the combined phenotype. Future trials should include people with cognitive impairment, standardize sarcopenia definitions, measure rehabilitation exposure and adherence, and test whether targeting the combined phenotype improves patient-centered outcomes.

titre: Effectiveness of dynamic neuromuscular stabilization-based interventions for nonspecific low back pain: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
auteurs: Ma Yuanyuan, Chen Yonghuan, Seo Jae Chul, Kim Hyun-Tae, Ma Jing, Jin Chengzhu
resume: Nonspecific low back pain (NLBP) is a leading cause of disability and imposes substantial public health and socioeconomic burdens. Dynamic Neuromuscular Stabilization (DNS) is increasingly used in NLBP rehabilitation, but quantitative evidence of its effects remains limited. We systematically reviewed and meta-analyzed controlled trials evaluating DNS-based interventions for NLBP. PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, and CNKI were searched. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data. Random-effects meta-analysis, subgroup analyses, and leave-one-out analyses were performed using Review Manager 5.4 and Stata 17.0. Potential small-study effects were examined using Begg's rank-correlation test. Eight studies involving 289 participants were included. The pooled analysis favored DNS-based interventions for pain-related outcomes (SMD = -1.17, 95% CI: -1.85 to -0.48), but heterogeneity was substantial (I2 = 85%). Subgroup analyses by intervention strategy, duration, weekly frequency, and session duration did not clearly account for the heterogeneity and were considered exploratory. Begg's test yielded p = 0.063, but the assessment of publication bias and small-study effects was inconclusive given the limited evidence base. Leave-one-out analysis indicated that no individual study alone materially altered the pooled estimate, but it did not resolve the remaining clinical and methodological uncertainties. DNS-based interventions may reduce pain-related outcomes in individuals with NLBP; however, the magnitude, clinical importance, and generalizability of the effect remain uncertain. Adequately powered, high-quality RCTs using standardized DNS protocols, clearly defined comparators, and consistent pain-specific outcomes are needed. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, PROSPERO (No. CRD420251152728).

titre: Dry needling combined with percutaneous electrical stimulation using a needle-surface configuration for musculoskeletal pain: A systematic review.
auteurs: Tzigkounakis Giorgos, Simati Katerina, Stefanakis Manos, Herrero Pablo
revue: Acupuncture in medicine : journal of the British Medical Acupuncture Society
resume: To systematically review the evidence on percutaneous electrical stimulation delivered via a needle-surface electrode configuration for musculoskeletal pain. PubMed and Scopus were searched, with additional screening of Google Scholar, from January 2010 to January 2026. Eligible studies included adults with musculoskeletal pain receiving percutaneous electrical stimulation delivered via a needle-surface electrode configuration. Primary outcomes were pain intensity and pain-related disability. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation criteria. Due to heterogeneity, a narrative synthesis was used to summarise the findings. Four randomised controlled trials involving 150 participants were included. All studies examined myofascial neck pain involving upper trapezius myofascial trigger points. Pain generally improved over time in both the intervention and comparator groups. Needle-surface stimulation showed selected short-term advantages over only dry needling, but superiority was not consistent across outcomes or follow-up periods. Disability improved in some trials without clear between-group differences. Certainty of evidence for pain and disability was low. Percutaneous electrical stimulation delivered via a needle-surface electrode configuration may improve pain-related outcomes in myofascial neck pain, but current evidence does not show consistent superiority over active comparators. Mechanistic and biophysical studies are needed to determine whether the needle-surface configuration produces clinically meaningful differences in current distribution, tissue recruitment and neuromodulatory effects when compared with other electrical stimulation configurations.
type_etude: Essai contrôlé randomisé (détection par mots-clés, à confirmer)

titre: Work-related musculoskeletal pain, fatigue, and dietary habits in athletic trainers and physical therapists providing sports team support.
auteurs: Jen Yu-Ching, Chang Wen-Hsin, Chang Nai-Jen
resume: BackgroundAthletic professionals (athletic trainers and physical therapists) perform injury prevention, health management, evaluation, emergency care, post-injury protection, rehabilitation, and administrative duties. Their focus on athletes' health may lead them to overlook high physical and psychosocial demands that may increase musculoskeletal pain (MSP), fatigue, and unhealthy dietary habits.ObjectiveTo examine MSP, fatigue, and dietary habits among athletic professionals who provide on-site team support and explore how fatigue and dietary habits relate to MSP.MethodsParticipants were required to be athletic professionals providing on-site team support. This cross-sectional online survey assessed 3-month work-related MSP in body regions, fatigue using a modified Fatigue Assessment Scale, and dietary habits using a structured food-frequency questionnaire. Logistic regression and mediation analyses examined associations and indirect associations, adjusting for relevant confounders.ResultsA total of 132 valid responses were included. MSP was highly prevalent, particularly in the lower back (83%), wrists/fingers (80%), and neck (67%). Fatigue (OR = 3.1, 95% CI = 1.34-7.45) and several suboptimal dietary habits (e.g., irregular meal timing, inadequate intake, fast eating, unbalanced diet, replacing meals with snacks, emotional eating) were significantly associated with MSP. Exploratory mediation analyses indicated statistically significant indirect associations via inadequate intake, replacing meals with snacks, and emotional eating, suggesting these behaviours may partially account for the fatigue-MSP association.ConclusionsAthletic professionals experience a high burden of MSP, fatigue, and suboptimal dietary habits that may be interrelated in ways that exacerbate work-related health. Workplace strategies should address workload, fatigue management, and access to healthy eating options to support sustainable practice and well-being.
type_etude: Étude observationnelle (détection par mots-clés, à confirmer)

titre: Financial burden, non-medical drivers of health, and early caregiving role formation after stroke: a scoping review.
auteurs: Okpala Munachi, Flake-Rojas Mariel, Akomaning Edwin, Woodall Shelby, Simpkins Alexis, Chukwuekezie Okechukwu, Oladunjoye Layomi, Sharrief Anjail Z
resume: Family caregivers are essential to stroke recovery, yet existing assessments may not adequately capture structural factors influencing caregiving capacity. Financial toxicity, non-medical drivers of health (NMDOH), and caregiver role formation during early post-stroke recovery remain poorly characterized. This scoping review evaluated how current caregiver assessments address these domains. A scoping review using the Arksey and O'Malley and Levac frameworks was reported according to PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Four databases were searched for studies published within the past 10 years examining informal caregiving during hospitalization, inpatient rehabilitation, or early transition home after stroke. Data were extracted on caregiver assessments, financial toxicity, NMDOH, and caregiver role formation. Sixteen studies were included. Assessments commonly capture caregiver burden, psychosocial distress, preparedness, social support, and caregiving tasks. Financial toxicity was absent in seven studies; most others assessed only subjective financial strain or a single objective indicator, such as income loss. Only one study assessed financial toxicity multidimensionally, incorporating income loss, direct costs, and debt. Employment and healthcare access were the most frequently assessed NMDOH domains (11 studies each), while housing and transportation were less frequently addressed; food security was absent. All studies addressed aspects of caregiver role formation, most commonly preparedness, but only one examined its relationship with financial toxicity. Caregiver assessments inconsistently capture financial toxicity and NMDOH. Future instruments should integrate multidimensional financial toxicity and NMDOH measures with caregiver role formation to better identify vulnerability and support equitable, sustainable stroke recovery.

titre: Early Changes in Post-Stroke Quality of Life and Associated Factors: A Prospective Study.
auteurs: Demir Yazici Senay, Birtane Murat, Tastekin Nurettin, Ekuklu Galip, Utku Ufuk, Turgut Nilda, Asil Talip
resume: BackgroundStroke affects physical, psychological, and social functioning. Early changes in health-related quality of life (HRQoL) remain incompletely characterized.ObjectivesTo assess early HRQoL changes after stroke and identify associated factors.MethodsWe assessed 111 patients with first-ever stroke at baseline, 1 month, and 3 months. Functional status, cognition, depressive symptoms, and HRQoL were evaluated using the Barthel Index, Functional Ambulation Scale, Mini-Mental State Examination, Beck Depression Inventory, Form-36 (SF-36) and the Stroke Impact Scale 3.0 (SIS 3.0). Paired tests, correlations with false discovery rate correction, and multivariable linear regression were used.ResultsNinety-seven patients completed follow-up. Physical and psychosocial HRQoL showed divergent recovery trajectories. SF-36 physical component scores progressively improved across both intervals (baseline to 1 month, p  =  0.006; 1 to 3 months, p = 0.033), whereas mental component scores improved only during the first month (p = 0.021) and showed no further significant improvement thereafter (p = 0.342). Similarly, SIS 3.0 emotion scores showed no significant change between 1 and 3 months (p = 0.831) and no significant net change over 3 months (q = 0.103), unlike the other domains, which continued to improve. In multivariable regression, functional ambulation at 3 months was independently associated with physical HRQoL change (β = 0.483, p < 0.001; adjusted R2 = 0.450), whereas depressive symptom severity was independently associated with mental HRQoL change (β = -0.692, p < 0.001; adjusted R2 = 0.667).ConclusionPhysical and psychosocial HRQoL did not recover in parallel during the first 3 months after stroke. Ambulation and depressive symptoms warrant separate attention during early rehabilitation planning.

titre: Delivery fidelity was high with variable uptake of optional components in a remote multicomponent rehabilitation intervention in intensive care unit survivors (iRehab): a mixed-methods fidelity assessment.
auteurs: Bradley Judy M, Ghiglieri Cara G, O'Neill Brenda M, Murphy Darren, Costley Jill, McAuley Daniel F, Connolly Bronwen A
resume: What was the fidelity of a remote multicomponent rehabilitation intervention in intensive care unit survivors (iRehab) across the National Institutes of Health Behavior Change Consortium Treatment Fidelity framework domains (design, training, delivery, receipt and enactment)? iRehab participants (n = 429; 231 intervention, 198 standard care); interviews involved 20 intervention participants, 15 standard care participants and six intervention staff. A mixed-methods fidelity assessment was embedded within the process evaluation of a multicentre randomised controlled trial. Quantitative fidelity was assessed using structured checklists, participant-level tracking data and longitudinal monitoring of potential drift. Qualitative interviews explored fidelity processes across domains. Study design fidelity was maintained, with clear differentiation between the experimental intervention and standard care. Provider training included structured training, competency assessment and ongoing multidisciplinary support. Delivery fidelity was high for one-to-one sessions, with no systematic drift in sampled sessions. Of 231 participants allocated to iRehab, 169 (73%) attended at least five one-to-one appointments. The uptake of optional group-based components was more variable. Qualitative findings indicated participant understanding and engagement, whereas tracking data and participant accounts provided evidence of strategies being applied in daily life. The iRehab intervention was delivered with high delivery fidelity while allowing individualisation to patient needs. For physiotherapists, monitoring of fidelity should extend beyond attendance and exercise prescription to whether patients can independently apply rehabilitation strategies when symptoms, fatigue and everyday demands fluctuate. Defined core components, staff training, staff competency assessment, ongoing support and fidelity monitoring may help support consistent remote delivery.

titre: Aspects of hand use development in infants aged 4 to 18 months with or at risk of cerebral palsy: a longitudinal study.
auteurs: Poulsen Helle Sneftrup, Hansen Alice Ørts, Laulund Lone Walentin, Ytterberg Charlotte, Rosenbek Minet Lisbeth
resume: Promoting hand use is a key goal in the rehabilitation of infants with or at risk of cerebral palsy (CP). To inform treatment planning, this study aimed to describe aspects of hand use development in these infants aged four to 18 months. Longitudinal design with repeated measurements using the Hand Assessment for Infants (HAI) from four to 12 months of age. At 18 months of age, the Assisting Hand Assessment (AHA), Both Hand Assessment (BoHA), Peabody Developmental Motor Scale (PDMS-2), and mini-MACS (Manual Ability Classification System) were applied. Descriptive statistics identified developmental trajectories for hand use. Linear mixed models estimated growth curves among infants diagnosed with CP. Associations between HAI scores at six and 8 months and outcomes at 18 months were examined using Spearman rank correlation and regression analyses. In total, 41 infants with or at risk of CP participated. Developmental hand use trajectories for each infant showed a clear pattern, with trajectories clustering according to manual ability at 18 months, classified by mini-MACS level for infants with CP (bilateral [n = 17], unilateral [n = 12]) and as "typical manual ability" for infants without CP (n = 12). Growth curve, defined by CP subtype and mini-MACS level at 18 months, showed modest differences between groups in the early months, relatively weak linear improvement in HAI scores over time in infants with higher mini-MACS, steeper gains over time in infants with lower mini-MACS, and a similar pattern with overlapping confidence intervals for the two CP subtype within the same mini-MACS level. A strong negative correlation was found between HAI scores and mini-MACS level. Regression analyses demonstrated a statistically significant and positive association between HAI scores and BoHA, AHA, or PDMS-2 subtest (Visual-Motor Integration) scores. HAI scores at 6 months of age may indicate the subsequent development of hand use up to 18 months of age. This contributes important knowledge to early treatment planning. The results must be interpreted with caution due to the small sample size. Larger studies are needed before firm conclusions are made.

titre: Anabolic responsiveness in critically ill children: a narrative review and conceptual perspective on nutrient utilization and muscle response.
auteurs: Giannakopoulou Ioulia, Ilia Stavroula, Briassoulis George, Raissaki Maria, Kozana Androniki, Filippatos Filippos, Kakleas Konstantinos, Miliaraki Marianna
resume: Critical illness alters energy metabolism, substrate use, and protein turnover in children, while skeletal muscle loss may continue despite apparently adequate energy and protein delivery. Nutritional adequacy may depend not only on nutrient delivery but also on how effectively nutrients are utilized to preserve muscle and support anabolic responsiveness. This hypothesis-generating narrative review synthesizes evidence on metabolic alterations and anabolic responsiveness in critically ill children, focusing on indirect calorimetry, respiratory quotient (RQ), non-protein RQ (npRQ), nitrogen balance, and quadriceps and diaphragm ultrasound. PubMed/MEDLINE was searched from inception to July 2026, prioritizing pediatric evidence and incorporating adult studies when pediatric data were insufficient. Indirect calorimetry remains the reference bedside method for measuring resting energy expenditure but cannot determine whether nutrients are incorporated into skeletal muscle protein. RQ and npRQ provide information on whole-body substrate oxidation but lack validated pediatric thresholds. Nitrogen balance estimates whole-body protein retention or loss but does not directly reflect skeletal muscle protein balance. Serial ultrasound can track regional muscle changes, although quadriceps and diaphragm measurements reflect different physiological influences. Pediatric studies demonstrate early peripheral muscle loss, while direct measurements of muscle protein synthesis and breakdown remain limited. No routinely available bedside method can directly assess anabolic responsiveness or confirm anabolic resistance. Integrating metabolic measurements with serial muscle assessment may identify mismatches between nutrient delivery and tissue response but remains hypothesis-generating. Prospective studies incorporating direct protein kinetics are needed to determine when anabolic responsiveness is restored and whether this can guide nutritional and rehabilitation strategies.

titre: Long-term functional outcome after post-anoxic brain injury: model development and internal validation from a multicentre cohort.
auteurs: Paolo Zanatta, Manuela Cattelan, Lucia Focella, Valentino Marchesan, Federico Linassi, Ernesto Gastaldo, Stefano Masiero, Elena Rossato, Alessandra Del Felice
revue: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
resume: To identify biomarkers of long-term functional recovery after cardiac arrest (CA). This is a prospective longitudinal cohort study based on the Veneto Registry of CA (July 2021- June 2023). We collected demographic, clinical, biochemical, and electroencephalography and short- and middle-latencysomatosensory-evoked-potentials (S-SSEP and ML-SSEP) within 72 hours. Functional scales were collected at discharge, 3, 6, and 12 months after the event. Multiple imputation was used to avoid statistical loss. Calibration was verified. A penalised logistic regression and a penalised continuation ratio were fitted to model the effect of covariates. The quality of prediction or fitting was verified computing the rank probability score for ordinal outcomes, the Brier score, and area under the ROC curve for binary outcomes. Decision curve analysis confirmed clinical utility. We included 160 persons (mean 62.80 ± SD 14.36 years; 123 males) out of 186. The interaction between continuous/nearly continuous EEG and N20/P25 predictor of survival (β = 0.840) and recovery (β = 1.160) of consciousness at 12 months after CA. ML-SSEP was a predictor of good outcome on all scales at 12 months after CA (0.739<β <1.708). ML-SSEPs associated with standard neurophysiological assessments are robust predictors of long-term functional outcomes after CA. ML-SSEPs associated with EEG and standard SSEP might be incorporated in routine clinical practice in ICU post-anoxic coma assessment.

titre: Haptic Connection to a Partner Enhances Motor Learning Retention in Older Adults: Implications for Multiplayer Robotic Rehabilitation.
auteurs: Waters Erica L, Meng Nova Y, Sobotka Natalia Stroutinsky, Shofer Frances S, Cacchione Pamela Z, Mendonca Rochelle J, Johnson Michelle J
revue: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
resume: There is a growing interest in understanding how haptic communication between individuals can improve motor learning, particularly in the context of robotassisted neurorehabilitation. Multi-user robotic systems can haptically connect patients, caregivers, and/or clinicians, providing an implicit communication channel and increasing engagement through multiplayer games. Previous studies of haptic communication and motor learning, however, have focused on pairs of healthy young adults completing relatively simple robot-based tasks. We present a study investigating older adults learning a 1-degree-of-freedom robot-based pursuit tracking task under two conditions: solo and dyad. We evaluated the evolution of motor performance in 38 trials with 1-week follow up. We found no between-group differences in tracking error at any time point. Within-groups, we observed significantly lower tracking error at both the same-day assessment and 1-week retention compared with baseline for both the more skilled and less skilled members of the dyads, whereas the solo group showed no significant improvements across trials. Learning curve analysis further demonstrated superior retention in the less skilled dyad partners relative to the solo group. During the interaction trials, the less skilled partner decreased their tracking error while the more skilled partner maintained performance. We also note exaggerated movements and increased effort from the more skilled partners in the dyads, which may suggest the emergence of a leader-follower dynamic. Together, these findings indicate that training with a haptic connection to a partner yields modest benefits for motor learning in older adults, with the strongest evidence for improved retention among the less skilled partners.

titre: Camera-Based AI-Assisted Scoring for the Balance Error Scoring System: A Cross-sectional Validity and Agreement Study.
auteurs: Chen Yushi, Cheng Jiayan, Wang Tsz Yuen Frank, Zheng Shanshan, Yu Le, Xue Xiao'ao, Sun Yang, Hua Yinghui
resume: The Balance Error Scoring System (BESS) is widely used to assess static postural control in sports medicine and rehabilitation. However, conventional real-time scoring is observer dependent and may be influenced by rater experience, viewing angle, attention, and the interpretation of transient or overlapping errors. This study evaluated the criterion-related validity and agreement of a camera-based artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted BESS relative to consensus video-review manual scoring and compared its error magnitude with on-site manual scoring. This single-center cross-sectional study included 80 of 84 recruited participants: 40 healthy controls, 20 with chronic ankle instability (CAI), and 20 after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR). All participants completed the standard six-condition BESS protocol. Scores were obtained using AI-assisted, on-site manual, and consensus video-review manual scoring; the latter was prespecified as the pragmatic manual reference standard. Primary total-score analyses included Pearson correlation, the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), Bland-Altman mean difference and 95% limits of agreement (LoA), mean absolute error (MAE), and root mean square error (RMSE). Condition- and group-specific analyses were exploratory. For the total BESS score, AI-assisted scoring versus the reference showed r = 0.989, ICC = 0.989 (95% CI 0.982-0.993), a mean difference of 0.188 errors, 95% LoA from -2.063 to 2.438 errors, an MAE of 0.787 errors, and an RMSE of 1.157 errors. On-site manual scoring versus the reference showed r = 0.922, ICC = 0.920 (95% CI 0.877-0.948), a mean difference of -0.612 errors, 95% LoA from -6.680 to 5.455 errors, an MAE of 2.212 errors, and an RMSE of 3.136 errors. Condition-specific discrepancies were larger in the single-leg and tandem-stance conditions. Exploratory group comparisons showed higher total BESS scores in individuals with CAI than in healthy controls. Camera-based AI-assisted BESS scoring showed strong total-score agreement with the pragmatic manual reference standard and smaller discrepancies than on-site manual scoring. This approach may support more standardized BESS assessment; however, external validation and longitudinal reliability testing are required before interchangeability with manual scoring can be considered.

titre: A wearable vibroarthrography system with PID-controlled negative-pressure suction and synchronized posture estimation.
auteurs: Lin Jiun-Hung, Tang Shih-Tsang
revue: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
resume: BackgroundVibroarthrography (VAG) is a non-invasive technique for evaluating joint health through acoustic signals generated during movement. However, reliable signal acquisition during dynamic activities remains challenging due to sensor displacement, motion artifacts, and inconsistent skin contact.ObjectiveThis study proposes an advanced wearable VAG system integrating PID-controlled negative-pressure suction and real-time posture estimation to improve signal stability and enhance the assessment of knee joint mechanics during movement.MethodsThe proposed system combines a wearable acoustic sensing module with a vacuum-assisted suction cup and a PID controller that consistently maintains sensor adhesion. Real-time posture estimation is achieved using MediaPipe Pose, which computes knee flexion angles. VAG signals and kinematic data are synchronously acquired during OKC and CKC exercises for integrated analysis.ResultsIn this single-subject pilot test, the system achieved stable sensor attachment and repeatable vibroacoustic recordings throughout dynamic movements. Distinguishable frequency-domain characteristics were observed at relevant knee flexion angles, including approximately 30°, 63°, and 129°.ConclusionsThis pilot feasibility study demonstrates that the proposed wearable VAG platform can achieve stable acquisition of synchronized vibroacoustic and kinematic signals during dynamic knee movement in a single subject. These preliminary findings suggest potential future applications in osteoarthritis screening, rehabilitation assessment, and ambulatory monitoring, pending validation in larger, statistically powered cohorts.

titre: Transcutaneous Vagus Nerve Stimulation Improves Motor Function of Upper Extremity in Adults with Chronic Ischemic Stroke: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
auteurs: Darwish Moshera H, El-Tamawy Mohamed S, Mostafa Marwa, Abo-Zaid Nehad A, Alenezi Sheemah, Khalifa Heba A
resume: BackgroundUpper limb motor dysfunctions are common after stroke affecting daily activities. About 60% of survivors still have impairment despite rehabilitation.ObjectiveTo assess the effect of transcutaneous auricular vagal nerve stimulation (taVNS) on upper limb motor function in chronic stroke patients.MethodsForty patients with chronic ischemic stroke in the middle cerebral artery territory were randomly assigned equally to; real group received 30 min of real taVNS followed by 30 min of upper limb exercises and sham group received identical program with sham taVNS. Intervention was conducted three sessions / week for four weeks. Upper extremity motor functions; Isometric (shoulder abductor, elbow flexors) and isokinetic (elbow flexors, extensors) muscle strength; and hand grip were evaluated through Fugl-Meyer Assessment for upper extremity (FMA- UE), Biodex system, and electronic hand dynamometer, respectively pre and post intervention.ResultsPost-intervention between-group comparisons favored real taVNS for FMA-UE (MD = 3.95, 95% CI 0.21-7.69), IMSA (MD = 4.78, 95% CI 1.89-7.66), IMEF (MD = 4.16, 95% CI 1.02-7.30), IKEE (MD = 5.34, 95% CI 3.23-7.61), and IKEF (MD = 4.72, 95% CI 2.71-6.72, p < 0.05). The HG improved significantly within the real taVNS group; however, the between-group difference was not significant (MD = 1.33, 95% CI -1.21 -3.85, p = 0.297).ConclusionstaVNS was associated with significant between-group improvements in upper-limb motor function and shoulder and elbow muscle strength. Clinical relevance of FMA-UE should be interpreted cautiously because its 95% CI was below the reported minimal clinically important difference.

titre: Rhythm-centred music interventions for motor coordination and rehabilitation: a scoping review of mechanisms, design principles, and technology-assisted assessment.
auteurs: Song Yongfan, Wei Yaming
resume: To map the evidence on rhythm-centred music interventions and movement-directed music-based strategies for motor coordination and rehabilitation, and to summarize their mechanisms, design principles, and technology-assisted assessment approaches. This scoping review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute framework and was reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and PsycINFO were searched for English-language empirical studies published from January 2013 to December 2024. Studies were eligible if music or rhythmically structured auditory input was used as a movement-directed intervention and at least one motor, coordination, functional, or movement-quality outcome was reported. Sixty-three studies were included. Coordination-related tasks were the most common targets, while lower-limb/gait function and fine-motor skills formed the largest movement categories. Rhythm was the most frequently used musical element, whereas melody, pitch, motivational music, active music making, and interactive digital systems served more context-dependent functions. Technology-assisted assessment, including sensors, motion capture, gait-analysis platforms, and music-interactive software, was the most common measurement approach. Rhythm-centred and music-based motor interventions are heterogeneous and should be interpreted as descriptive evidence patterns rather than definitive estimates of therapeutic efficacy. Future studies should improve terminology, intervention parameterization, population-specific interpretation, methodological transparency, and multimodal mechanistic validation.

titre: Bothersome and activity-limiting pain in community-dwelling older adults with versus without stroke: a cross-sectional analysis of the National Health and Aging Trends study (2011-2024).
auteurs: Venkata Reddy Shivananda, Mathew Aby, Dombrowsky Thomas, Ramachandran Arunachalam, Hariharan S, Chandrakumar K
resume: Stroke and pain are common health challenges among older adults. However, limited research has examined the burden of pain among community-dwelling older adults with a history of stroke in the United States of America (USA). This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of bothersome and activity-limiting pain and examine the association between stroke history and pain outcomes among older adults in the USA. This cross-sectional secondary analysis used publicly available data from Rounds 1-14 of the National Health and Aging Trends Study (NHATS), conducted from 2011 to 2024. The study included adults aged ≥ 65 years and compared participants with and without a self-reported physician-diagnosed history of stroke. Pain outcomes were derived from standardized NHATS interview data and included bothersome pain and activity-limiting pain. Demographic, clinical, psychological, physical, and sleep-related variables were obtained from the NHATS dataset. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression was used to examine the associations between stroke history and pain outcomes after adjustment for relevant covariates. Among 12,797 participants, 2,235 (15.71%) had a history of stroke, and 10,562 (84.29%) did not. The prevalence of bothersome pain was higher among participants with stroke than among those without stroke (60.77% vs. 54.66%; p = .003). Similarly, activity-limiting pain was more prevalent among participants with stroke (62.83% vs. 52.00%; p < .001). After adjustment for demographic, clinical, psychological, physical, and sleep-related factors, stroke remained independently associated with bothersome pain (OR 1.30, 95% CI 1.02-1.66; p = .034) and activity-limiting pain (OR 1.20, 95% CI 1.04-1.38; p = .013). Pain represents a substantial burden among U.S. older adults with a history of stroke. Stroke was independently associated with both bothersome and activity-limiting pain, highlighting the importance of comprehensive pain assessment and management within geriatric stroke rehabilitation.

titre: Conus Medullaris Syndrome Following Traumatic Thoracolumbar Burst Fractures: Clinical Presentation, Surgical Management, and Early Outcomes in Three Cases.
auteurs: Ajay R, Anand B Vijay, Rishab C, Delish Dhanush, Raj R Rohit
resume: Burst fractures of the thoracolumbar spine can carry a neurological deficit, particularly where the conus medullaris is injured. Conus medullaris syndrome (CMS) typically disturbs bladder, bowel, and sexual function while sparing much of the leg power, and its earliest signs are easily missed. We report three patients in whom a traumatic thoracolumbar burst fracture produced features of CMS and describe their operative management. A 57-year-old man with an L1 burst fracture and intact leg power presented with bowel and bladder incontinence and underwent posterior stabilization (D11-L3), regaining continence early. A 25-year-old man with an L1 burst fracture and sacral involvement after a fall from height had impaired voiding and defecation with blunted S3-S5 sensation and was treated with L1 decompression with stabilization (D12-L2). A 62-year-old woman with a 2-month-old D12 nonunion, paraparesis, and multilevel disc protrusion underwent D10-L2 transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion. All three patients demonstrated neurological improvement after surgical decompression and stabilization. Early recovery of bladder function occurred in one patient, while the remaining two experienced symptomatic improvement with ongoing rehabilitation. Thoracolumbar burst fractures involving the T12-L2 region may compress the conus medullaris, resulting in a spectrum of neurological deficits ranging from isolated sphincter dysfunction to mixed upper and lower motor neuron signs. Early recognition requires careful neurological examination, particularly assessment of sacral sensation and sphincter function, and early magnetic resonance imaging and prompt posterior decompression with fixation favor recovery, though return of bladder and sphincter function stays unpredictable.

titre: The S-technique: A Novel Dense Polytetrafluoroethylene-assisted Surgical Technique for Peri-implant Keratinized Mucosa Preservation - A Case Review.
auteurs: Nettemu Sunil Kumar, Nettem Sowmya, Nayak Vijayendranath, Kannaiyan Karthik, Bharathwaj V V
resume: Immediate implant placement following tooth extraction often leads to peri-implant defects that require guided bone regeneration (GBR) to achieve complete bone fill and stable osseointegration. Conventional GBR techniques typically rely on primary flap closure, coronal advancement, and additional soft-tissue grafting, which increase surgical complexity and patient morbidity. The S-Technique was introduced to enable simultaneous hard and soft-tissue regeneration under open-healing conditions while preserving the mucogingival junction. A patient presented with a grossly decayed, painful, vertically fractured, nonrestorable maxillary right second premolar (tooth 15). After atraumatic extraction and immediate implant placement, a peri-implant gap defect with limited soft-tissue availability was noted. GBR was performed using particulate xenograft and a resorbable collagen membrane. A dense polytetrafluoroethylene membrane was then placed according to the S-technique protocol, allowing secondary epithelialization without primary closure. Healing progressed uneventfully. At 4 months, clinical assessment showed complete coverage of the peri-implant site, an adequate band of keratinized mucosa, improved soft-tissue contour, a favorable emergence profile, and stable peri-implant architecture. Prosthetic rehabilitation resulted in satisfactory esthetic and functional outcomes with maintained bone support. This case demonstrates the S-Technique as a minimally invasive dual-layer membrane approach for simultaneous hard and soft-tissue regeneration around immediate implants. By eliminating the need for primary closure and autogenous soft-tissue grafting, it offers a predictable alternative for managing peri-implant defects in sites with limited soft-tissue availability, while promoting keratinized mucosa formation and stable peri-implant tissue integration.

titre: Osteochondral lesions of the talus in the pediatric population: A practical narrative review.
auteurs: Turati Marco, Gatti Simone Daniel, Thüsing Monika, Guelfi Matteo, Crippa Marco, Sinikumpu Jaakko, Bigoni Marco
resume: Osteochondral lesions of the talus (OLTs) in children and adolescents are a clinically important cause of persistent ankle pain after trauma and may also be present without a clear inciting event. Because plain radiographs may fail to detect OLTs or may underestimate their severity, modern pediatric pathways rely on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for characterization. However, conventional MRI may be inconclusive regarding osteochondral fragment stability in selected cases. In this setting, magnetic resonance arthrography may provide additional information, although pediatric-specific evidence is limited and its routine use is not supported. Nonoperative management is commonly used as first-line treatment for stable lesions in skeletally immature patients, but reported success is variable and often modest, prompting increasing interest in standardized conservative protocols and prospective comparisons. When surgery is required, selection among retrograde drilling, bone marrow stimulation, and fragment fixation is primarily driven by osteochondral fragment stability, cartilage integrity, fragment viability, and the extent of subchondral bone involvement. Assessment should also include ankle stability because clinically relevant concomitant ligamentous instability may influence treatment selection and outcomes. When ligament stabilization is indicated, minimally invasive arthroscopic techniques may be considered. Cartilage restoration and graft-based techniques may be indicated for large or cystic lesions, high-stage lesions, or revision cases, though pediatric-specific long-term evidence remains limited. This review summarizes contemporary assessment, imaging, treatment options, rehabilitation principles, and long-term considerations to support evidence-informed clinical decision-making.

titre: Prediction of late-pregnancy pelvic floor dysfunction: a nomogram model based on proton density fat fraction and synthetic magnetic resonance imaging.
auteurs: Zeng Yanni, Wang Juanting, Shi Haiyan, Guo Ruomi, Zhao Xueying, Li Yan, Zhou Yu, Wu Hongsheng, Hong Yong
revue: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
resume: Pelvic floor dysfunction (PFD) is a highly prevalent condition that significantly compromises women's quality of life. To date, the majority of studies and clinical rehabilitation interventions have focused on the assessment and management of pelvic floor muscle (PFM) function in the postpartum period, whereas investigations into the monitoring of pelvic floor function during the third trimester of pregnancy remain relatively understudied. This study aimed to develop a radiology-clinical nomogram integrating proton density fat fraction (PDFF; Iterative Decomposition of water and fat with Echo Asymmetry and Least-squares estimation, IDEAL-IQ sequence), synthetic magnetic resonance imaging (MAGnetic Resonance Image Compilation, MAGiC sequence), and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) for predicting PFD in late pregnancy. A total of 114 third-trimester pregnant women were classified into PFD and non-PFD groups. Fat fraction (FF), T1, T2, proton density (PD), and fractional anisotropy (FA) of bilateral levator ani muscles (LAMs) were measured from IDEAL-IQ, MAGiC, and DTI by two radiologists (with 15 years of experience). Measurement reliability was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs). Univariate analysis screened potential predictors [age, gestational week, gravida, parity, delivery mode, fetal weight, pre- and post-pregnancy body mass index (BMI), and quantitative imaging parameters]. Significant variables were included in a multivariate logistic regression to build the nomogram. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Of 114 participants, 52 were assigned to the PFD group and 62 to the non-PFD group. Univariate analysis showed significant between-group differences in gestational week (P=0.025), gravida (P=0.032), parity (P=0.023), fetal weight (P<0.001), left LAM FF (L-LAM FF, P=0.005), and right LAM T2 (R-LAM T2, P=0.004). The final Akaike information criterion (AIC)-selected multivariable prediction model, gravida, L-LAM FF, and R-LAM T2 were retained as nomogram predictors. The nomogram achieved moderate discrimination with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.726 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.632-0.815]. Calibration indicated good model fit, and DCA demonstrated positive net benefit within a threshold probability range of 25-83%. Interobserver agreement was moderate/excellent (ICC 0.49-0.86). FA was only an exploratory imaging biomarker and was not retained in the final combined prediction model. The nomogram incorporating gravida, L-LAM FF, and R-LAM T2 effectively predicts PFD in late pregnancy.

titre: How does pre-stroke physical activity influence physical activity one year after minor stroke, and what role does cognitive impairment play?
auteurs: Knudsen Anne Meyer, Rolving Nanna, Mortensen Janne Kærgård, Damsbo Andreas Gammelgaard
resume: To examine the association between pre-stroke physical activity and physical activity levels 12 months after stroke, and to explore whether cognitive impairment modifies this association. This study was a secondary analysis of data from a prospective cohort study of 100 patients with stroke at Aarhus University Hospital. Physical activity was assessed using the Physical Activity Scale for the Elderly, and cognitive function was measured using the Repeatable Battery for the Assessment of Neuropsychological Status. Logistic regression analyses were performed to examine associations between pre- and post-stroke physical activity, adjusting for relevant covariates. Low pre-stroke physical activity had significantly higher odds of low physical activity 12-months post-stroke (OR = 5.81, 95% CI: 1.61-24.0, p = 0.010). The estimated odds ratio for effect modification by cognitive impairment was 7.44 (95% CI: 0.81-89.9, p = 0.092), although the wide confidence interval indicates substantial uncertainty. Pre-stroke PA was associated with PA levels 12 months post-stroke in individuals with mild stroke. Assessing pre-stroke PA may help identify patients at risk of persistent inactivity and guide personalized rehabilitation. The modifying role of cognitive impairment remains inconclusive and warrants further investigation.

titre: Time-Varying Social Integration and Long-Term All-Cause and Cause-Specific Mortality After Traumatic Spinal Cord Injury: A Longitudinal SCIMS Study.
auteurs: Calderone Andrea, Marra Angela, De Luca Rosaria, Mangano Alessandra, Sorbello Gabriele, Quartarone Angelo, Calabrò Rocco Salvatore
revue: Archives of physical medicine and rehabilitation
resume: To determine whether lower time-updated social integration and within-person decline are associated with subsequent mortality after traumatic spinal cord injury (SCI), and to examine cause-specific and educational gradients. Longitudinal secondary cohort analysis using annually lagged exposure, a 5-year validity window, and discrete-time survival models with participant-clustered standard errors. Spinal Cord Injury Model Systems 2021 public-use database. Adults with traumatic SCI and at least one eligible Craig Handicap Assessment and Reporting Technique (CHART) Social Integration assessment. The primary cohort included 16,783 participants; the repeated-assessment model included 6,610 participants, entering follow-up after their second assessment. Not applicable. All-cause mortality was primary. Natural-cause, external-cause, and suicide mortality were secondary; suicide was a subset of external causes. CHART and education were exposures or covariates. During 122,626 exposure-covered person-years, 2,965 deaths occurred. Crude mortality increased from 17.3 per 1,000 person-years at CHART 100 to 46.8 at CHART 0-49. Each 10-point lower current score was associated with higher mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 1.09; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.07-1.10). A lower first score (HR, 1.078; 95% CI, 1.049-1.108) and within-person decline (HR, 1.077; 95% CI, 1.051-1.104) were associated with mortality per 10 points. Associations were observed for natural (HR, 1.08) and external mortality (HR, 1.11); the suicide estimate was imprecise (HR, 1.05; 95% CI, 0.96-1.15). Lower education corresponded to higher standardized 10-year mortality risk. Estimates were similar when the first assessment occurred within two years of injury. Primary cause was unavailable for 23.2% of deaths, and early postinjury mortality was incompletely represented in follow-up. Lower and declining social integration were associated with higher subsequent mortality after traumatic SCI. Repeated assessment may provide prognostic information, but survivor selection, missing causes, and residual confounding limit interpretation. These findings do not establish that modifying social integration or education changes survival.

titre: Validation of a Revised V-Slope Algorithm for Automated First Ventilatory Threshold Detection in Healthy Adults.
auteurs: Vermeiren Margot, Goetschalckx Kaatje, Van Opstal Herwig, Claes Jomme, Van Langenhoven Leen, Cauwenberghs Nicholas, Willems Rik, Ntalianis Evangelos, Kuznetsova Tatiana, Cornelissen Veronique, Sinnaeve Peter
resume: The first ventilatory threshold (VT1) is a key indicator of submaximal aerobic fitness. Its determination typically relies on visual assessment, which is time-consuming and subject to interobserver variability. Automated solutions may offer a more objective, reproducible and time-efficient alternative. This study evaluated the accuracy of a revised V-slope method. This retrospective study was conducted at University Hospitals Leuven, Belgium, using cardiopulmonary exercise test (CPET) data of 271 healthy adults collected between 2010 and 2020. Automated VT1 detection using a revised V-slope algorithm was compared with manual determination via the visual V-slope method in 262 participants with a determinable VT1. Agreement was evaluated using Bland-Altman analysis, intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), Deming regression and equivalence testing (TOST). Interobserver agreement was evaluated using ICC. Median oxygen uptake at VT1 was higher with automated compared to manual assessment (1151 vs. 1122 mL/min; p < 0.001). Mean difference was 29 mL/min (95% CI [19, 40]. Relative mean bias was 2.2% ± 7.1% (LoA [- 11.7 to 16.0%], with excellent agreement (ICC 0.97 [95% CI 0.96-0.98] and a Deming regression slope of 0.95 [95% CI 0.92-0.99] and intercept of 26.1 mL/min [95% CI -11.9 to 64.7]. TOST with equivalence bounds [- 100, 100] was significant (p < 0.001; 90% CI [20, 38]). The revised V-slope algorithm demonstrated strong group-level agreement with visual assessment for VT1 determination, supporting the reliability and practical applicability for large-scale research applications in healthy adults. However, given the observed individual-level variability, caution is warranted when applying automated VT1 values to guide exercise prescription for individual patients without expert review.

titre: Virtual reality and VR-like technologies for the assessment and rehabilitation of concussion-related vestibular and oculomotor dysfunction: a systematic review.
auteurs: Kalal Dhirenbhai, Hassny Syeda Maryam
resume: Vestibular and oculomotor dysfunction after concussion may cause persistent dizziness, imbalance, visual motion sensitivity, and functional limitation. Virtual reality (VR) and technologies are used for assessment and rehabilitation, but applications, devices, and outcomes remain heterogeneous. This review evaluated VR and VR-like technologies for concussion-related vestibular and oculomotor dysfunction. Following PRISMA 2020 and PROSPERO registration, CENTRAL, MEDLINE, PsycINFO, PubMed, and Scopus were searched from inception to 21 March 2026. Of 1,197 records, 997 remained after deduplication; 55 full texts were assessed and 10 studies included. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data. Owing to heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively. One study evaluated VR-based rehabilitation and nine examined assessment, validation, or symptom provocation. Rehabilitation outcomes improved across conventional, VR-based, and hybrid therapy groups, without consistent superiority of VR. Assessment studies suggested that standardized visual-motion environments may reveal postural, sensory-integration, or symptom-provocation responses not evident during static testing. However, findings varied by technology, recovery stage, task, and outcome. Eye-tracking showed poor diagnostic discrimination, and visual perturbation did not consistently demonstrate concussion-related impairment. VR may be a useful adjunct for standardized, repeatable, ecologically relevant assessment and rehabilitation, but evidence does not support stand-alone use or superiority over conventional therapy.

titre: Nanoparticles in the Diagnosis and Management of Stroke: A Review.
auteurs: Furqan Muhammad, Qureshi Muhammad Qasim, Huda F N U, Azhar Hiba, Younus Shaheera, Sohail Saad, Sattar Saba, Rahim Sadia Binte, Haider Muhammad Usman, Khalid Mazhar, Butt Bilal, Phirke Tejas, Kamel Peter
resume: Stroke is the third leading cause of death and the fourth leading cause of disability-adjusted life years worldwide, yet disease-modifying treatment remains largely confined to reperfusion of large-vessel ischemic occlusion within a narrow window. No neuroprotective or hemostatic agent has entered routine practice. Engineered nanoparticles have been proposed to improve delivery across the blood-brain barrier, concentrate drug within the ischemic or perihematomal microenvironment, and add imaging or sensing functions. The resulting literature is large but fragmented across platforms, models, and outcome measures, so it is not evident which platforms carry the strongest evidence or which are closest to clinical evaluation. This narrative review synthesizes preclinical and clinical evidence on nanoparticle-based diagnosis, treatment, rehabilitation, and monitoring in ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke. We searched PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library from inception to July 2025 using predefined Boolean strings and assigned each included study an evidence tier to separate extrapolated and cross-field evidence from stroke-specific data. Comparative tables summarize nanoparticle type, payload, model, route, dose, treatment window, particle size and surface charge, principal outcomes, safety assessment, and translational readiness. Therapeutic evidence is almost entirely preclinical: Efficacy has been shown in young, male, comorbidity-free rodents treated within minutes of reperfusion and followed for 24 h to 28 days, with group sizes typically between three and 15, and few studies reporting any bleeding or coagulation endpoint. Diagnostic applications are closer to patients because iron-oxide nanoparticles have already been given to humans, although not for imaging. We identified seven registered clinical studies of nanoparticle-related interventions in stroke; one perfluorocarbon nanodroplet emulsion completed a randomized dose-escalation trial in acute ischemic stroke, the EU Clinical Trials Register returned none, and none exists in hemorrhagic stroke. Nanoparticle platforms, therefore, remain investigational, and progress will depend less on new chemistry than on comorbid and large-animal models, realistic treatment windows, systematic reporting of bleeding risk and of interference with follow-up imaging, and reproducible manufacturing.

titre: Cross-cultural adaptation and validation of the Traditional Chinese NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX) for assessing perceived workload in Taiwanese adults.
auteurs: Chung Shih-Chi, Hsieh Meng-Chen, Chiao Chia-Yi
resume: BackgroundPerceived workload is central to occupational health, ergonomics, and rehabilitation research, yet no guideline-based Traditional Chinese version of the NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX) has been available for Taiwan and other Traditional-Chinese-speaking settings.ObjectiveTo cross-culturally adapt the NASA-TLX into Traditional Chinese (NASA-TLX-TC) and evaluate its measurement properties in Taiwanese adults.MethodsIn a psychometric secondary analysis, 114 community-dwelling adults aged 20-50 years completed the NASA-TLX-TC on three consecutive days. Within the COSMIN framework, we examined content validity, internal consistency, structural validity (exploratory factor analysis with parallel analysis), test-retest reliability (intraclass correlation [ICC]), measurement error, and construct validity (seven a priori hypotheses involving sleep, mood, and shift work).ResultsThe content validity index averaged 0.88 and Cronbach's α was 0.83. The six dimensions loaded on a single factor (55.8% of variance). The three-day average score showed good reliability (ICC[A,k] = 0.83), whereas single-day reliability was moderate (0.62); the minimal detectable change was 32 points. Six of seven construct-validity hypotheses were supported; the shift-work difference was in the predicted direction but nonsignificant. Internal consistency and convergent validity were stable across subgroups.ConclusionsThe NASA-TLX-TC showed good reliability and initial construct validity and is suitable for group-level occupational-health, ergonomics, and rehabilitation research; multi-day averaging is recommended for individual assessment.
