titre: Acceptability of two smart mobility aids: perspectives of healthcare professionals and management working in long term care settings.
auteurs: Best Krista L, Cézé Estelle, Dandois Marie, Piette Patrice, Letoullec Elodie, Lefort Mathilde, Routhier Francois, Leblong Emilie, Fraudet Bastien
resume: Two smart walking aid aids were conceptualised to respond to mobility needs of older adults, including a Walker with Intelligent and Safe Navigation (DENIS), and an Individual Vehicle with Intelligent Verticalization and Navigation Aid for Autonomy (VIVIANA). The aim of this study was to explore perceived acceptability of DENIS and VIVIANA among healthcare professionals (HCPs), specifically exploring factors that influence intention to use. An exploratory multi-method study was conducted. Acceptability of the concepts for DENIS and VIVIANA were explored among HCPs working in LTC settings. HCPs completed the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) questionnaire to explore performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence and facilitating conditions. Semi-structured individual and group discussions were used to descriptively nuance the same constructs. Correlations and multivariate regression analyses were conducted to explore predictors of intention to use and future use. Individual and group discussions were narratively summarised. Thirty-nine HCPs with 15.3 ± 9.2 years of experience completed the UTAUT and participated in individual or group discussions. HCPs reported high acceptability and intention to use both technologies in the future. Intention to use DENIS was predicted by profession and social influence, while effort expectancy was the main predictor of intention to use VIVIANA. Both smart mobility aids were deemed acceptable by HCPs. Practical considerations such as training, cost, and maintenance highlight the importance of actively involving HCPs in the design and implementation of these technologies in LTC settings.

titre: [From clinical practice to interventional study : Adaptation of a local approach to therapeutic and rehabilitative care to a complex intervention in the "SGB Reha" project].
auteurs: Desch Anke K, Häusler Andreas, Förstner Bernd R, Deeken Friederike, Artmann Jörg, Altin Sibel, Dierbach Oskar, Boutmans Charlotte, Beckmann Olaf, Schleich Laura, Nitzschke Nikola, Siegert Sarah, Hommel Aileen, Schroth Jennifer, Du Manuel, Mierzwa Nora, Gradel Björn, Hauptmann Michael, Rapp Michael, Holmberg Christine
resume: Therapeutic-rehabilitative care aims to promote the independence, quality of life and social participation of people in need of care through multiprofessional collaboration and therapeutic interventions. Transforming practice-based concepts into interventions that can be scientifically evaluated requires an understanding of their mechanisms of action and the necessary adaptations to new care contexts. This paper reconstructs the transformation process of a therapeutic-rehabilitative care concept into the intervention of the project "SGB Reha". The goal is to provide a clear account of the adaptations made during this process. The basis for the intervention concept was a theory of change model which was further refined in collaboration with stakeholders through a participatory and iterative process. Requirements regarding implementability, evaluability and contextual conditions, were taken into account. Additional resources, frequency and design of measures were adjusted, while central mechanisms of action were retained and made explicit in the action model. The development process illustrates the necessary balance between standardization and context-sensitive adaptation. The transition of a care concept to an evaluable intervention was an iterative transformation process. The action model supported the systematic adaptation and made assumptions, mechanisms of action, and adjustments transparent. The development of complex interventions requires a balance between preserving core principles of effectiveness and adapting them to new contexts. The experiences from SGB Reha demonstrate how a practice-based concept can be transformed in a theory-guided manner into a scientifically evaluable intervention.

titre: Effects of thoracic kinesiological taping on pulmonary functions, respiratory muscle strength, and functional independence in patients with hemiplegia: a randomized controlled clinical trial.
auteurs: Bitmani Natali, Günday Çiçek, Tütüneken Yunus Emre, Soltanalizadeh Roya
resume: To investigate the effects of thoracic kinesiology taping (KT) on pulmonary function, respiratory muscle strength, and functional independence in individuals with chronic post-stroke hemiplegia. 30 patients were randomly assigned to a thoracic KT or sham taping group. Both groups received conventional rehabilitation 5 days/week for 4 weeks. The KT group received thoracic taping with 50-75% tension, whereas the sham group received an identical application without tension. Outcomes were assessed at baseline and post-intervention, and included forced vital capacity (FVC), forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1), peak expiratory flow (PEF), maximal inspiratory pressure (MIP), maximal expiratory pressure (MEP), and Functional Independence Measure (FIM). Both groups showed significant within-group improvements in FVC, FEV1, PEF, and MIP (all p = 0.001), with greater changes in the KT group. FIM improved significantly only in the KT group (p = 0.015). MEP did not change in the KT group (p = 0.674) but showed a small increase in the sham group (p = 0.010). Between-group comparisons demonstrated significant advantages in favor of KT for FVC (p < 0.001), FEV1 (p < 0.001), PEF (p < 0.001), and MIP (p < 0.001) and FIM (p = 0.029), while a small but significant advantage in MEP was observed in favor of the sham group (p = 0.030). Thoracic KT, when combined with conventional rehabilitation, significantly improves pulmonary function and inspiratory muscle strength in individuals with chronic stroke. Its effects appear to be primarily related to optimization of ventilatory mechanics rather than direct muscle strengthening. Thoracic KT may serve as a practical adjunct in respiratory neurorehabilitation.

titre: Potential roles of sperm-associated tsRNAs in offspring alkaline tolerance in grass carp (Ctenopharyngodon idella).
auteurs: Zhu Chao, Pan Weiping, Zheng Jianbo, Liu Shili, Chi Meili, Jiang Wenping, Cheng Shun, Peng Miao, Luo Junzhi, Li Fei, Zhang Haiqi
resume: Transfer RNA-derived small RNAs (tsRNAs) are emerging epigenetic regulators involved in environmental adaptation and paternal effects. Their roles in fish offspring alkaline tolerance, however, remain unclear. In this study, small non-coding RNA (sncRNA) profiles of grass carp (Ctenopharyngodon idella) sperm, oocytes, and embryos were characterized by high-throughput sequencing, and the potential functions of sperm-associated tsRNAs were further investigated. Significant differences in sncRNA expression profiles were observed among sperm, oocytes, and embryos, with tsRNAs representing the most abundant sncRNA class in all groups. Most tsRNAs originated from the nuclear genome and were mainly classified as tiRNA-5, showing biased expression patterns derived from only a few specific tRNAs. A total of 36 tsRNAs were detected exclusively in sperm and embryos but were not detected in oocytes, suggesting potential paternal delivery during fertilization. Integration with alkaline stress-responsive data further identified 18 candidate tsRNAs associated with both alkaline stress response and potential paternal contribution. Predicted target genes were significantly enriched in pathways related to stress response, ion homeostasis, epithelial remodeling, and energy metabolism. Functional microinjection assays in zebrafish and grass carp embryos showed that tRF-33-R9JP9PMNH5SYDQ and tRF-33-KQI34JRX6N380Q significantly enhanced offspring survival under alkaline stress, whereas inhibition of these tsRNAs reduced alkaline tolerance. These findings suggest that sperm-derived tsRNAs may participate in regulating offspring alkaline tolerance in fish and may provide candidate molecular targets for future alkaline-tolerant breeding programs.

titre: Gesture-based rehabilitation as an assistive technology for post-infectious and post-critical illness disabilities: opportunities and challenges.
auteurs: Ali Muhammad Usman, Ghumman Ujala Nauman, Raja Maryam Shakeel, Noor Ezza, Ramzan Fahad
resume: This commentary examines gesture-based rehabilitation (GBR) as an assistive technology within an ecosystem for survivors of infectious diseases with neurological disabilities. It describes the roles of computer vision, markerless motion capture, depth cameras, artificial intelligence-driven pose estimation, wearable sensors, smartphone-based tracking, and virtual or augmented reality, while considering infection control and global accessibility. This commentary was developed by synthesising the existing literature, with an emphasis on camera-based motion capture, gesture-controlled serious games, AI-driven pose estimation, wearable movement sensors, smartphone tracking, and virtual or augmented reality rehabilitation systems. The analysis compares outcomes from traditional neurological conditions, such as stroke and Parkinson's disease, to the specific needs of infectious disease survivors. Evidence from stroke, Parkinson's disease, and other neurological populations suggests that gesture-based systems may support motor rehabilitation, patient engagement, and remote monitoring. GBR may also reduce the need for direct patient-therapist interaction. However, there is currently insufficient direct evidence on the effectiveness, safety, and feasibility of these systems among survivors of infectious diseases. Additional barriers include hardware costs, limited digital infrastructure, and unequal access in rural and resource-constrained settings. GBR offers a versatile method for aiding recovery after infectious neurological illnesses. Nonetheless, its safety, effectiveness, and practicality in these groups remain uncertain, as most evidence comes from non-infectious neurological conditions. Specific studies on these populations are necessary before routinely recommending these technologies, along with strategies to overcome technological, financial, and access-related challenges.

titre: Graduate Students Trapped Between Pressures and Screens: A Multi-Wave Longitudinal Network and Cross-Lagged Panel Study.
auteurs: Ma Peng, Wen Zhonglin, Meng Jin, Wang Yifan, Chen Shisi, Zhang Linke, Liu Xiqin
revue: Stress and health : journal of the International Society for the Investigation of Stress
resume: Chinese graduate students face multiple pressures from academic, familial, social, and personal sources, like academic learning inefficiency (difficulty completing research tasks), campus unfamiliarity (poor environmental adaptation), and certification pressure (obligation to obtain professional credentials). That may drive many to overuse short-form videos as a coping strategy. However, how these pressures dynamically relate to video overuse over time remains unclear. We conducted a three-wave longitudinal study (N = 2471) using Network analysis, Cross-Lagged Panel Network Analysis (CLPN), and Random Intercept Cross-Lagged Model (RI-CLPM). Results revealed three findings. First, across all three waves, strong associations existed between learning inefficiency and campus unfamiliarity, as well as between the ideal-reality gap (discrepancy between expected and actual graduate life) and social adjustment. Central nodes were mainly certification pressure and parental expectations. Second, CLPN indicated that short-form video overuse showed the strongest autoregressive edge; the strongest cross-lagged edge was from social pressure to personal stress. School pressure appears to have had a stronger impact on other variables at the subsequent time point, while both school pressure and family pressure appear to have exerted a greater contemporaneous influence on other variables. School pressure and family pressure may have subsequently increased short-form video overuse. Last, RI-CLPM indicated that higher overall pressure levels significantly predicted increased video overuse at the next wave, but the reverse effect was non-significant. Implications include prioritising certification pressure and parental expectations, proactive school pressure management, and addressing video overuse by targeting its pressure drivers rather than the behaviour itself.

titre: Population Genomic Survey of Dongliao Black and Jilin Spotted Pigs and Their Genetic Relationships With Northeastern Asian Breeds.
auteurs: Zhang Xiaoran, Bai Chunyan, Chen Changyi, Dong Fengyi, Li Jing, Jin Long, Ning Jiayi, Feng Chengyue, Bie Luyao, Wang Dali, Sun Hao, Niu Wei, Sun Boxing
resume: In this study, we conducted a population genomic survey of two local pig breeds in Jilin Province, Dongliao Black (DLB) and Jilin Spotted (JLS) pigs, and evaluated their genetic relationships with 23 Northeastern Asian pig breeds, comprising 46 wild boars, 211 Chinese local pigs, 69 Russian pigs, 13 Korean pigs, and 107 commercial pigs. The results will be helpful for the conservation and utilization of these rare germplasm resources. The minor allele frequency of DLB and JLS pigs was 0.24 and 0.22, respectively. Both DLB and JLS pigs exhibited higher observed heterozygosity than expected values. Moreover, JLS pigs displayed the lowest excess of homozygosity inbreeding coefficient (-0.12 ± 0.07) among all studied populations. Additionally, population structure analyses indicated that DLB and JLS pigs possess admixed ancestries intermediate between Chinese and Western pigs, with DLB being closely related to Min pigs and both breeds showing admixture signals with neighboring Northeastern Chinese breeds, reflecting their distinct hybrid histories. Furthermore, 16 and 19 genes were identified as putative candidate genes in DLB and JLS pigs using Fst analyses, respectively. All these findings are consistent with a history of crossbreeding and with low levels of inbreeding in DLB and JLS pig populations. Additionally, it is hypothesized that DLB and JLS pig breeds may carry putative candidate genes during their breeding programs, which are associated with meat quality, reproduction, production, immunity, and environmental adaptation. Therefore, strengthening conservation and promotion efforts for DLB and JLS pigs is of great significance.

titre: Comply or don't fly: Airport security screening experiences of people who have limb loss and limb difference.
auteurs: Burnell Aaron, Finco M G, Keller Olivia, Doyle Whitney, McDonald Cody L
resume: People who have limb loss (amputation etiology) or limb difference (congenital etiology) can experience additional challenges with airport security screening due to their assistive device or prosthesis. However, perspectives on airport security screening from people with limb loss and limb difference remain unreported. This survey elicited experiences of airport security screening in the United States from people who have limb loss and limb difference to inform recommendations for the Transportation Security Administration. The Amputee Coalition conducted an anonymous online survey. Close-ended questions (demographics, frequency of and satisfaction with airport security screening) and three open-ended questions (experiences with airport security screening) were analyzed using descriptive statistics and inductive codebook reflexive analyses. Of respondents (n = 288) who provided demographics, most were White (n = 218; 83%), 55+ years of age (n = 148; 56%), had one leg or foot affected (n = 214; 80%), use a prosthesis (n = 245; 93%), or use a wheelchair (n = 84; 61%). Nearly half experienced 2-5 airport security screenings in the past year (n = 79; 49%). A third were satisfied (n = 83; 31%) with TSA agents. Five themes were developed: 1) screenings are excessively time consuming, 2) treatment from TSA agents is dehumanizing, 3) policies and TSA agents are inconsistent, 4) responsibility to educate TSA agents, and 5) dread flying due to TSA experiences. To address these concerns, TSA should develop and require training that includes people who have limb loss and limb difference, as well as provide more detailed information on the TSA Cares website.

titre: AR-glass-assisted drone operation for wheelchair users: an experimental comparison of operation modes.
auteurs: Uhm Jun-Phil, Kim Sanghoon, Lee Seungmin
resume: As an initial psychological and user-experience evaluation of accessible drone use, this study experimentally compared three drone-operation modes, line-of-sight, conventional screen-based, and AR-glass-assisted operation, among wheelchair users and examined their effects on presence, escapism, and state subjective vitality. A between-subjects experiment was conducted with wheelchair users who had no prior drone-control experience. Participants were assigned to line-of-sight, conventional screen-based, or AR-glass-assisted drone operation. All participants received standardised training and completed an outdoor drone-operation task using the same drone model, flight route, task instructions, operation time, and safety procedures. Presence, escapism, and state subjective vitality were measured immediately after the task. Personal innovativeness with technology was included as a covariate, and the data were analysed using multivariate analysis of covariance and Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise comparisons. Drone-operation mode significantly influenced the combined experiential outcomes. AR-glass-assisted operation produced the highest levels of presence, escapism, and state subjective vitality, followed by conventional screen-based operation and line-of-sight operation. The differences among operation modes were consistent across all three outcomes. AR-glass-assisted drone operation may provide wheelchair users with a more immersive and psychologically meaningful leisure experience. Integrating the drone's visual perspective into a wearable field of view appears to strengthen presence, psychological escape, and immediate vitality, suggesting that drone-mediated AR may support remote environmental exploration as a form of accessible leisure without being framed as a substitute for physical mobility or accessible built environments.

titre: Impact of augmented reality on narrative-related outcomes in children with Autism Spectrum Disorder: a within-subject design.
auteurs: Berenguer Carmen, Fuentes-Sáez Cristina, Baixauli Inmaculada, Andrés Ma de El Puig, Gómez-García Soledad
resume: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is commonly associated with impairments in social communication, narrative abilities, and socio-cognitive functioning. This study explored whether augmented reality (AR) could enhance narrative production, comprehension, use of mental state language, and reading-related behaviors in children with ASD. Fifteen children with ASD without intellectual disability participated in a within-subjects design in which they completed story retelling tasks under two counterbalanced conditions: a traditional paper-based format and a tablet-based format. Narrative performance was assessed through measures of microstructure, including productivity, lexical diversity, and syntax, as well as macrostructure indicators such as recall of main ideas. Oral comprehension and reading-oriented behaviors were also examined. Results showed that the AR condition significantly improved socio-cognitive and behavioral outcomes. Children produced a higher number of mental state terms and demonstrated greater attention, persistence, and engagement during the tasks. These findings suggest that AR can function as an effective scaffold that facilitates the explicit representation of internal states while increasing attentional involvement. Consequently, AR technology may represent a promising tool for improving language assessment and fostering social-cognitive development in children with ASD.

titre: Exploring the participation of people with lower limb absence or amputation: a mixed methods study.
auteurs: Pousett Brittany M, Battalova Alfiya, Parag Nishtha, Cumming Donna, Welch Kassandra A, Rapaport Malena Sofia, MacKay Crystal, Miller William C
resume: People with lower limb absence or amputation (LLA) face challenges in their ability to participate in their communities. This study examines what influences how people with LLA participate in meaningful activities and social roles within the context of British Columbia. We used a sequential mixed methods design consisting of 48 semi-structured interviews and 114 survey responses. Qualitative data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Quantitative data included Ability to Participate in Social Roles and Activities Questionnaire and Prosthesis Evaluation Questionnaire Ambulation subscale. Multiple regression explored predictors of participation. Participants demonstrated participation impairment, with restrictions in mobility, sport and exercise. Ambulation was the strongest predictor of participation, followed by female sex. Five themes described factors shaping participation: physical abilities and assistive technology (including prosthesis use); built and natural environments; social relationships; access to prosthetic care, peer support, and adaptive sport; and coping strategies. Physical challenges and funding limitations intensified barriers, while appropriate prosthetic treatment, social support, and mindset facilitated participation. Participation among people with LLA is influenced by interconnected physical, environmental, social, systemic, and psychosocial factors. Prioritizing mobility, improving funding equity, enhancing access to prosthetic care, and supporting psychosocial wellbeing may reduce participation restrictions.

titre: Assessment of pathogenic traits in selected bacteria isolated from snowy environments in France and Greenland.
auteurs: Kashiri Masoumeh, Zervas Athanasios, Brill Florian H H, Steinmann Jörg, Neumann Bernd, Mogrovejo Diana C, Anesio Alexandre M
resume: Microorganisms inhabiting cold environments have gained increasing attention in recent decades due to their unique adaptation mechanisms that enable survival under extreme conditions. Growing evidence indicates that some cold-adapted bacteria possess phenotypic and genomic traits linked to pathogenicity, raising concerns about their potential environmental and public health relevance. Here, we characterized three culturable bacteria isolated from human-impacted snow in the French Alps (Chamrousse) and coastal Greenland (Nuuk). Snow samples were cultured on R2A medium, and isolates were identified by Sanger sequencing as Peribacillus, Sphingomonas, and Subtercola. Temperature tolerance, haemolytic activity, and antibiotic susceptibility were assessed by culture-based assays, while whole-genome sequencing was used to screen for antibiotic resistance and virulence-associated genes using reference databases. Only the Peribacillus isolate tolerated 37 °C and showed α-haemolysis. Antibiotic susceptibility testing indicated full susceptibility in Peribacillus, while Sphingomonas and Subtercola showed reduced susceptibility to a limited number of antibiotics, mainly to cefotaxime, chloramphenicol, and colistin. Genomes encoded genes associated with efflux, target modification, motility/adhesion, and stress adaptation, indicating environmental resilience rather than clinical pathogenicity. Overall, these isolates displayed limited pathogenic phenotypes with genomic traits primarily supporting environmental adaptation and survival.

titre: Integrated analysis uncovers the role of circadian rhythm genes in cold adaptation of Kandelia obovata using the multi-omics data.
auteurs: Xu Chaoqun, Wang Ji-Cheng, Sun Ling, Ma Dong-Na, Ding Qian-Su, Song Ling-Yu, Li Jing, Zhuang Li-Han, Zhu Xue-Yi, Lu Haoliang, Chen Luzhen, Chen Guangcheng, Lu Changyi, Zheng Hai-Lei
resume: Kandelia obovata and Kandelia candel, two sister mangrove species within the genus Kandelia (Rhizophoraceae), exhibit pronounced differences in cold tolerance. However, the genetic basis underlying this adaptive divergence remains unclear. In this study, we assembled a high-quality, chromosome-level genome of K. candel (~225 Mb) to facilitate comparative genomic analysis with K. obovata. Functional enrichment revealed that expanded gene families in K. candel and contracted families in K. obovata were both significantly associated with transcription factor (TF) activity, highlighting TFs as potential key drivers of adaptive evolution. Using whole-genome resequencing data from 53 accessions across representative geographic ranges, we investigated population structure and identified genomic loci associated with environmental adaptation in K. obovata. Notably, temperature-responsive TFs were found to be involved in the circadian rhythm pathway. Through integrated genomic and transcriptomic analysis, we prioritized 18 circadian rhythm-related TFs, including PIF3, CCA1, LHY, and MYB family members such as PAP1, as high-priority candidates linked to cold adaptation in K. obovata. Enrichment analysis of the target genes regulated by these TFs further underscored the importance of flavonoid and phenylpropanoid metabolism under cold stress. Our results suggest that circadian rhythm genes, through their regulation of specialized metabolism, represent promising candidate regulators that may contribute to cold adaptation of K. obovata. This study provides not only key insights into the evolutionary mechanisms of mangrove cold resilience but also a valuable genomic resource for guiding conservation and assisted migration strategies under climate change.
theme: Aides techniques et adaptations de l'environnement

titre: Integrative genotype-environment association and single-cell transcriptomic analyses identify candidate mechanisms of environmental adaptation in pigs.
auteurs: Li Dong, Yuan Tiantian, Li Xiang, Quan Yu, Tian Xuekai, Cheng Ye, Wang Yulong, Wu Xinglong, Sun Boyuan, Liu Wansheng, Jiang Yu, Ding Rongrong, Groenen Martien A M, Derks Martijn F L, Yu Taiyong
resume: As one of the earliest domesticated and most globally ubiquitous livestock, pigs (Sus scrofa) have undergone profound environmental adaptation while following human expansion across diverse bioclimatic zones. Despite their evolutionary significance, the genomic mechanisms enabling pigs to thrive in disparate ecological settings remain poorly understood. Here, we present a comprehensive global analysis using a dataset of 1,151 pig genome sequences representing 146 distinct populations. By integrating three complementary genotype-environment association (GEA) frameworks including Redundancy Analysis (RDA), BayPass, and Latent Factor Mixed Models (LFMM), we identified genomic regions and candidate genes associated with environmental variation. Our analysis detected several candidate genes associated with high-altitude adaptation, particularly those involved in ultraviolet radiation response. By integrating lung single-cell RNA sequencing analysis (scRNA) from high-altitude and commercial breeds, we identified ASXL1 as a candidate gene potentially involved in high-altitude adaptation. Meanwhile, scRNA revealed candidate regulatory pathways, including the NOTCH signaling pathway, that were overlooked by traditional GEA methods, suggested the complex regulatory landscape of physiological adaptation. Together, this study integrates large-scale population genomics and scRNA to provide insights into the genetic associations and regulatory landscapes potentially contributing to environmental adaptation in domestic pigs, advancing our understanding of livestock evolutionary responses to diverse ecological conditions.

titre: Mapping the proteome landscape in Euglena gracilis: global, phospho, and ubiquitin proteomes under anaerobic response.
auteurs: Tamaki Shun, Nishino Kohei, Ezoe Akihiro, Minami Anzu, Kim June-Sik, Firdaus Ade Rizqi Ridwan, Subroto Toto, Kosako Hidetaka, Mochida Keiichi
resume: The photosynthetic flagellate Euglena gracilis (Euglena) exhibits a remarkable metabolic flexibility, enabling the dynamic coordination of energy production and resource partitioning during anaerobic adaptation. While the wax ester synthesis under hypoxia is well-documented, the regulatory interplay between protein abundance and post-translational modifications (PTMs) remains unexplored. A definitive understanding of this metabolic remodeling is hindered by the lack of high-depth proteomic resources and the fragmented genome annotations, which fail to capture Euglena's proteomic diversity and plasticity. Here, we provide a comprehensive Euglena proteome landscape through advanced LC-MS/MS analysis. By leveraging the recently refined proteome annotation, we identified 9,122 protein groups, 12,027 phospho-peptides, and 3,346 ubiquitinated peptides, establishing a comprehensive Euglena's proteome reference. Our results demonstrate that anaerobic adaptation is characterized by distinct phosphorylation and ubiquitination signatures that often occur independently of changes in global protein abundance, revealing a layer of PTM-mediated control over central metabolism during anaerobic adaptation in Euglena. This study provides a foundational resource that bridges the gap between genomic potential and functional metabolic in Euglena. By resolving the interplay between protein levels and PTM-driven regulation, our work offers a new resource for investigating environmental adaptation and provides a rigorous framework for future metabolic engineering in Euglena.

titre: National burden of disabilities in Bangladesh and its socio-demographic correlates: A 2021 cross-sectional analysis.
auteurs: Rahman Mizanur, Rana Md Shohel, Khandaker Gulam, Rahman Md Mostafizur, Khan Md Nuruzzaman
resume: Disability remains an important public health and social challenge, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), including Bangladesh. However, nationally representative evidence on its burden, distribution, and associated factors remains limited. This study estimated the national prevalence and patterns of disability in Bangladesh and examined their sociodemographic correlates. This cross-sectional study analysed data from 155,025 participants in the 2021 National Survey on Persons with Disabilities (NSPD). Disability status (yes or no) was the primary outcome. Explanatory variables were measured at the individual, household, and community levels. Multilevel mixed-effects logistic regression models, stratified by age group (0-17 years [children] and 18-95 years [adults]), were used to examine factors associated with disability. The prevalence of disability was 2.79% (95% CI 2.69-2.91). Physical disability (42.44%) and visual impairment (14.11%) were the most commonly reported types, and 11.60% of persons with disabilities reported multiple disabilities. Overall, disability was more prevalent among males, although sex-specific patterns differed by age. Among children, girls had 31% higher adjusted odds of disability than boys (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.31, 95% CI 1.13-1.52), whereas no significant sex was observed among adults (aOR 1.06, 95% CI 0.95-1.19). In both age groups, the odds of disability increased with years of schooling and household wealth. Among adults, housewives, students, and blue-collar workers had higher odds of disability than agriculture workers. Higher community-level literacy was associated with higher odds of disability among adults, whereas the association was reversed among children. The findings support strengthening community-based disability identification and referral in Bangladesh through existing primary health-care services, particularly in underserved populations and areas. Coordination between the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and the Department of Social Services could improve access to existing social protection, rehabilitation, and assistive-device services.

titre: Divergent adaptive strategies of different biological soil crusts to seasonal environmental fluctuations in a temperate desert.
auteurs: Han Z, Huang Y, Zhou W, Yang A, Zhang Q, Zhang S, Zhang W, Zhuang W, Ma F, Zhou X, Zhang Y, Ma X, Yin B
resume: Pronounced seasonal fluctuations in Central Asian temperate deserts, where annual temperature variations can exceed 80 °C, have shaped unique environmental adaptation strategies in regional vegetation. However, it remains unclear how biological soil crusts (BSCs), a dominant desert land cover, respond to inter-seasonal hydrothermal fluctuations and whether these adaptive strategies are consistent across different crust types. This study investigated cyanobacterial, lichen and moss crusts in the Gurbantunggut Desert to explore their seasonal adaptive strategies from the perspectives of biomass dynamics and non-structural carbohydrate (NSC) allocation patterns. The results indicated that biomass in cyanobacterial and lichen crusts increased progressively from spring to the following spring, whereas moss crusts showed no significant variation. Regarding resource allocation, cyanobacterial crusts showed a steady increase in soluble sugars and the soluble sugar-to-starch ratio, suggesting they effectively utilize seasonal precipitation pulses to sequester carbon (C) for growth. In contrast, lichen and moss crusts exhibited an inverse relationship between soluble sugars and starch; specifically, during stress periods, they remobilize starch into soluble sugars to maintain cellular osmotic homeostasis. Notably, their environmental tolerances diverged: lichen crusts exhibited high thermal tolerance but were sensitive to low-temperature stress, whereas moss crusts demonstrated robust chilling tolerance but were vulnerable to heat stress. In conclusion, our findings confirm that different BSC types employ distinctive survival strategies and stress-tolerance mechanisms, suggesting a potential for seasonal ecological niche complementarity. This study provides novel insights into the physiological adaptation strategies of desert cryptogams in response to extreme environmental variability.

titre: Long-term use of an assistive exercise product in young people with cerebral palsy who are non-ambulant is a balancing act-a phenomenographic study.
auteurs: Gårdling Jenny, Lauruschkus Katarina, Tornberg Åsa B
resume: According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), children should be physically active, including exercise, for 60 min a day, and limit sedentary behaviour across the week regardless of physical disabilities. Children with cerebral palsy who are non-ambulant (CP-NA), with Gross Motor Function Classification System Expanded & Revised IV to V, are known to be sedentary up to 92% of the time they spend awake and are dependent on assistive technology and assistive exercise products (AEP), such as the Innowalk. The aim of this study is therefore to explore the family and professional caregivers' perceptions of the long-term use of the AEP after three to five years of use. An inductive phenomenographic design was used, with the aim of describing and understanding variations in how individuals perceive a phenomenon; i.e., what something is and how something is perceived. 11 family caregivers and one professional caregiver to 11 young people (11-24 years) with CP-NA were interviewed individually using a semi-structured interview guide, after having used the AEP for three to five years. The analysis of the interviews followed the iterative steps of phenomenographic design. Long-term use of the AEP was described by caregivers as a life-long project involving balancing between maintaining control and aspects that were beyond their control in everyday life to provide physical activity and exercise in the AEP. When the caregiver managed to reach such a balance, and were able to provide physical activity and exercise in the AEP, it was experienced as rewarding, creating a feeling of meaningfulness. Long-term use of the AEP requires substantial caregiver coordination and support from surrounding services. When such support is available, the AEP may contribute to meaningfulness and improved quality of life for both the young person and their caregivers.

titre: Structural variation in the IAMH2 3' UTR underlies hypocotyl elongation during light adaptation in Arabidopsis thaliana.
auteurs: Gao Xuemeng, Chang Wenli, Liu Xuejing, Yao Yingjun, Song Yan, Yan Jin, Yang Kai, Liu Jianquan, Liu Huanhuan
revue: The Plant journal : for cell and molecular biology
resume: Plant hypocotyls are central to seedling establishment in variable light environments. Although core photoreceptor pathways regulating hypocotyl elongation are well defined, the molecular basis of natural variation in this trait-particularly through posttranscriptional regulation-remains poorly understood. Here, we report that a high-altitude, high-light-adapted Arabidopsis ecotype from Tibet exhibits longer hypocotyls under low light compared to a low-altitude ecotype from Sichuan. Using recombinant inbred lines combined with fine-mapping and near-isogenic line validation, we identified the major locus LA1 (Light Adaptation 1) and pinpointed IAMH2 as the causal gene. Full-length transcriptomics revealed a natural structural variant in the IAMH2 3' UTR of high-altitude ecotypes that alters its length and disrupts a poly(U) motif. We further show that in low-altitude ecotypes, the RNA-binding proteins C3H14/C3H15 directly bind this poly(U)-rich region to posttranscriptionally downregulate IAMH2 mRNA levels, thereby attenuating IAMH2-dependent IAA accumulation and hypocotyl elongation. Analysis of 38 globally representative ecotype genomes confirmed that IAMH2 3' UTR variation correlates with light intensity and elevation, supporting its role in environmental adaptation. Collectively, our work reveals a previously unknown C3H14/C3H15-IAMH2 posttranscriptional module that dynamically adjusts hypocotyl elongation in response to light, providing new insights into the plasticity and adaptive evolution of seedling photomorphogenesis.

titre: Redox regulation of plant hormone signaling transduction.
auteurs: Jing Peng-Wei, Li Song-Qi, Chen Bo-Hao, Wu Ji-Xiao, Li Lin, Liao Cai-Yi, Yang Hong, Lu Kai-Kai, Song Ru-Feng, Liu Wen-Cheng
resume: Plants need to precisely coordinate growth and development with stress responses under constantly changing environmental conditions, and the interaction between redox signaling and plant hormone signaling is an important regulatory mechanism underlying this balance. Reactive oxygen species (ROS) are not only oxidative metabolic products generated under stress conditions, but also important second messengers that modulate protein functions through oxidative post-translational modifications (oxi-PTMs). Recent studies have shown that ROS can directly regulate plant hormone signaling transduction through oxi-PTMs. By altering the activity, stability, subcellular localization, or protein interactions of hormone receptors, protein kinases, phosphatases, transcription factors, or hormone metabolic enzymes through redox modifications, ROS regulate the biosynthesis and signaling outputs of multiple hormones, including auxin, abscisic acid (ABA), brassinosteroids (BR), jasmonic acid (JA), salicylic acid (SA), ethylene (ET), and cytokinin (CK). In turn, plant hormones can reshape ROS homeostasis by regulating ROS-producing or -scavenging systems, thereby forming complex bidirectional feedback networks. ROS can also act as common signaling nodes among different hormone pathways to integrate plant growth and development with stress responses. This review summarizes the molecular mechanisms by which redox signals regulate plant hormone signaling transduction, with particular emphasis on the roles of protein redox modifications in hormone perception, signal transmission, and multi-hormone interactions, and discusses the potential of exploiting key redox-sensitive sites for precise crop improvement, with the aim of providing a new theoretical basis for understanding plant environmental adaptation and breeding stress-resistant, high-yielding crops.

titre: Beyond Foxp3 and TSDR: a dual epigenetic lock framework for treg stability and plasticity.
auteurs: Wang Feng, Yang Haiying, Xu Zhiguo, Song Jingxian, Wang Zijun, Wang Le
resume: Regulatory T cells (Tregs) maintain immune homeostasis by balancing lineage stability with functional adaptability. Although Foxp3 is central to Treg identity, Foxp3 expression alone does not fully explain the long-term maintenance of suppressive function or the capacity of Tregs to adapt to diverse tissue environments. Similarly, Foxp3 TSDR demethylation provides a durable epigenetic imprint but does not account for the dynamic regulation of broader Treg functional programs. Here, we propose the Dual Epigenetic Lock framework as a conceptual and testable model in which two complementary epigenetic layers contribute to Treg state regulation. The first lock consists of stable TSDR demethylation, which preserves lineage-associated Foxp3 expression competence. The second lock is proposed to involve Treg-associated super-enhancer networks that may stabilize suppressive transcriptional programs, regulate environmental adaptation, and constrain inappropriate inflammatory activation. This framework suggests that Treg stability emerges from the integration of durable lineage memory and dynamic functional regulation rather than from a single molecular determinant. Disruption of this balance may contribute to impaired immune tolerance in autoimmune diseases, whereas excessive reinforcement of suppressive regulatory programs may support tumor immune evasion. However, the extent to which these two epigenetic layers are mechanistically coupled remains unresolved. Emerging approaches including single-cell multi-omics, spatial epigenomics, and targeted epigenome engineering provide opportunities to test whether the dual-lock architecture predicts Treg state transitions and therapeutic responsiveness. This framework also provides a conceptual basis for two complementary therapeutic strategies: reinforcing Treg stability for immune tolerance and selectively modulating tumor-associated Treg programs for cancer immunotherapy.

titre: Literature-derived criteria and expert-perceived influence structure for age-friendly living environments among older adults living with HIV in China: a text-mining, fuzzy Delphi, and fuzzy DEMATEL study.
auteurs: Wen Quan, Zhang Jing, Ismail Mazran, Abdul Nasir Muhammad Hafeez, Wu Yanting
resume: Older adults living with HIV (OALHIV) may experience the demands of long-term HIV care together with frailty, stigma, privacy concerns, and barriers in their residential environment. This study developed an exploratory set of age-friendly living-environment criteria and examined how experts perceived influence among the resulting domains. It did not test epidemiological causality or measure regional service performance. An English-language Web of Science corpus covering 2003-2023 was processed with term co-occurrence mapping and clustering. Fuzzy Delphi method (FDM) ratings from 28 experts were used to screen candidate criteria, followed by domain-level fuzzy decision-making trial and evaluation laboratory (FDEMATEL). Sensitivity analyses examined the FDM cutoff and fuzzy-attitude parameter, and FDEMATEL was calculated using the standard zero-diagonal convention. The workflow included 1,487 records, 89 cleaned terms, 43 second-round candidates, and 22 retained criteria in five domains. The second-round mean FDM threshold was 0.4729. The same 22 criteria were retained for fixed thresholds from 0.453 to 0.478, for recalculated fuzzy-attitude parameters from 0.40 to 0.60, and under leave-one-criterion-out recalculation. In the zero-diagonal FDEMATEL analysis, healthcare accessibility (D-R = 0.320), social support network (0.683), and digital inclusion and assistive technology (0.866) occupied net-influencing positions; built-environment adaptation (-1.170) and psychological wellbeing and destigmatization (-0.699) occupied net-influenced positions. The sign classification matched the originally reported calculation, although magnitudes changed. The framework is hypothesis-generating and reflects literature-derived concepts and expert judgement, not demonstrated causal effects or the directly reported priorities of OALHIV. Patient and community co-design, field measurement, and external validation are required before the criteria can guide resource allocation.

titre: Assistive device usage among children living with cerebral palsy: parents' knowledge and perspective on its availability and usage at the Greater Accra Regional Hospital, Ghana.
auteurs: Osei Comfort Ama, Bawah Richard Kwaku, Aryiku James Nii Amar, Obuobi-Darko Felix, Baarkoh Crescensia, Agudu Agnes Delali
resume: Assistive devices can benefit a wide range of people, including those living with disabilities; those affected by severe forms of disease or trauma; and those requiring rehabilitation. Access to these devices is limited in low- and middle-income countries. The study explored parents' perspectives on the availability and use of assistive devices among children with cerebral palsy at the Greater Accra Regional Hospital in Ghana. An explorative qualitative research design was employed, with purposive sampling used in recruiting parents of children with cerebral palsy. Data were collected through in-depth, face-to-face interviews using a semi-structured interview guide. Data were analysed through thematic analysis. Three main themes emerged: (1) parents' knowledge and understanding of assistive devices, (2) parents' experiences of children's usage of assistive devices, and (3) availability and accessibility of assistive devices for children with cerebral palsy. Participants demonstrated basic knowledge of assistive devices, mainly identifying mobility aids such as wheelchairs and walkers. While some expressed satisfaction with the benefits of these devices, others were dissatisfied with the limited range and lack of advanced technologies. Significant barriers to access were identified, including limited availability, complex acquisition processes, delays in obtaining devices, and high costs. The study concludes that, among children with cerebral palsy, access to assistive devices is constrained not only by the availability of the devices but also by a mismatch between children's individual functional needs and the type, affordability, and accessibility.

titre: Patient Travel Experiences for Methadone Dosing Visits.
auteurs: Austin Elizabeth J, Ravi Varuna, Gojic Alexander J, Bhatraju Elenore P, Darnton James, Grekin Paul, Soth Sean, Woolworth Steve, Hallgren Kevin A, Tsui Judith I, Williams Emily C
resume: Patients often experience travel-related barriers to methadone dosing at opioid treatment programs (OTPs), but the nature of their experiences are not well understood. To characterize patient experiences with travel to OTPs for regular methadone dosing visits at a large multisite OTP in Washington state. This qualitative study utilized an embedded mixed-methods design. Our sample included patients currently receiving methadone treatment at 2 OTP sites in Washington state from November 2024 to February 2026 (including mobile units that operated as extension of the sites). Data were analyzed between February and July 2026. Experiences of travel to OTPs for regular, in-person observed methadone dosing. Results of a survey administered to patients regarding the modality, time, and cost (eg, gas, childcare) of traveling to the OTP. A subsample of surveyed patients were interviewed about their experiences with and perspectives on traveling for dosing visits. Survey data were analyzed descriptively. Interviews were coded using rapid assessment process. Our sample included 98 survey participants and 16 qualitative interview participants (median [IQR] age, 43.0 [38.8-50.3] years; 8 cisgender women [50.0%]). Among survey respondents, 54 (55.1%) drove themselves to the OTP, 21 (21.4%) were driven by another person, 12 (12.3%) took public transportation, and 6 (6.1%) took insurer-sponsored medical transportation; 18 (18.4%) reported a disabling condition and 16 (16.2%) needed an assistive device for walking. Participants spent a mean (range) 82.5 (10.0-330.0) minutes round trip and $15.80 ($0-$200.00) in travel-related costs for each visit. Qualitative interviews illuminated that, while distance was often a barrier, unpredictable OTP wait times or conflicts with work, medical, or family obligations also mattered considerably. Participants shared that dosing visits directly prohibited their ability to work, but missing visits put participants at risk for return to opioid use and treatment stagnation. In this mixed-methods qualitative study, requiring regular visits for in-person observed methadone dosing presented significant structural barriers that affect patients' treatment experience, adherence, and lives. Increasing the flexibility and accessibility of methadone treatment-through policies and novel care practices that actively seek to minimize burden of travel to the OTP and destigmatize care-is essential to enhance care quality and equity.

titre: Long-term provision and follow-up of assistive technology in post-humanitarian emergency contexts: a scoping review.
auteurs: Cole Ellie, Austin Victoria, Kett Maria
resume: Access to assistive technology (AT) is critical in humanitarian settings, yet availability remains extremely limited. Despite crises becoming more frequent and protracted, little is known about the situation beyond the acute emergency phase. This scoping review examines existing evidence on long-term AT provision and follow-up after the immediate response period. The review followed PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Six databases were searched, and publications focusing on AT in post-emergency, low-and-middle-income contexts published after 2015 were eligible. Of 487 records screened, only 16 met these criteria. A form was designed to record publication details, study characteristics and key findings. Data were interpreted using the WHO-GATE 5P framework (People, Policy, Products, Provision, Personnel). Findings reveal a lack of systematic AT provision in post-emergency settings. Services were often ad hoc, donor-driven, and focused on one-off device distribution. Mobility devices, particularly prostheses and wheelchairs, were most frequently reported, with studies largely situated in post-earthquake or refugee contexts. Barriers including cost, limited availability, and low-awareness persisted across settings. Contextual factors strongly shaped access and effectiveness, and unmet need varied widely between populations. Fragile health systems, restrictive policies, and trained personnel shortages further undermined long-term sustainability. This review highlights a significant evidence gap regarding long-term provision and follow-up of AT following humanitarian crises. Findings underscore the importance of context in shaping access and effectiveness during recovery, pointing to the need for integrated approaches linking humanitarian action with social protection systems to ensure sustained support and inclusion.

titre: Access to assistive technology for cerebral palsy: stakeholder and lived-experience perspectives from international focus groups.
auteurs: Auil María José, Coughlan John, Landre Anna, Kumar Gopi, Oldfrey Ben
resume: People with cerebral palsy (CP) face persistent barriers to accessing appropriate assistive technology (AT), despite its critical role in supporting health, independence, and participation. This study examines perspectives from people with CP, caregivers, rehabilitation professionals, AT developers, and disability-sector stakeholders to identify systemic barriers to AT access and explore priorities for strengthening AT systems globally. The aim is to inform the WHO-UNICEF Global Roadmap on Assistive Technology by integrating lived, professional, and system-level perspectives into policy and innovation discourse. Two sequential international virtual focus groups were conducted in March 2025 with 49 participants in the first session and 42 in the second, representing 20 countries across low-, middle-, and high-income settings. The first session explored challenges in AT access, and the second focused on potential solutions. Discussions were transcribed, anonymised, and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Analysis identified nine systemic barriers, including high costs, bureaucratic gaps, limited repair infrastructure, and exclusion from services in adulthood. Five priority areas emerged: localised production, technology-enabled customisation, strengthened service and workforce systems, cross-sector collaboration, and global peer learning. Grounding AT policy and innovation in participatory approaches that integrate lived experience alongside professional expertise can support more inclusive, resilient, and lifespan-oriented AT systems.

titre: CRISPR-Cas Tools for Dissecting and Engineering Environmental Responses in Microalgae.
auteurs: Zhao Wenyu, Li Xinyi, Hu Zhangli, Wang Song
resume: Microalgae are photosynthetic eukaryotes that need to maintain productivity under variable light, temperature, nutrient and CO<sub>2</sub> conditions, yet their complex regulatory networks have made relevant engineering difficult. Clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)-CRISPR-associated proteins (Cas) have changed the situation, shifting microalgal research from random transgene integration toward precise editing of the genes that mediate photosynthesis, stress responses and environmental acclimation. This work reviews how CRISPR-Cas has been applied across microalgal lineages to (i) dissect genes involved in stress response and photosynthesis, (ii) streamline genomes through large-scale deletions, (iii) build stress-tolerant chassis that retain photosynthetic performance under unsatisfactory conditions and (iv) reprogramme lipid, pigment and high-value compound pathways. We then discuss the determinants of editing efficiency, including single-guide RNA design, Cas nuclease choice and engineering, species-specific delivery, host physiology (cell-wall architecture, cell cycle phase and stress-induced repair-pathway shifts) as well as screening workflows using endogenous markers and high-throughput phenotyping. We propose that integrating species-specific multi-omics analyses, artificial intelligence-assisted design and precise and controllable editing strategies will further enhance the ability of CRISPR-Cas systems to elucidate photosynthetic regulatory networks and environmental response mechanisms in microalgae, while facilitating the optimisation of microalgal metabolic traits and the engineering of environmental adaptability.

titre: Comparative efficacy of digital health intervention delivery modalities on quality of life, anxiety, and depression in coronary heart disease: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
auteurs: Zhang Yiran, Yu Tianyou, Huang Wenrui, Tian Lin, Li Mutong, Wang Jiangbo, Li Zhaofeng
resume: Nonadherence to traditional cardiac rehabilitation and persistent psychological distress among patients with coronary heart disease (CHD) severely undermine desired therapeutic outcomes. Digital health interventions (DHIs) emerge as promising strategies to effectively tackle this adherence and mental health issue remotely. The aim of this study was to conduct a network meta-analysis (NMA) to compare and rank the comparative efficacy of various DHI delivery modalities in improving quality of life (QoL), anxiety, and depression among patients with CHD. A systematic search strategy was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane, CNKI, VIP, WanFang, and SinoMed databases to search for randomized controlled trials (RCTs)published from their inception to February 1,2026.We carried out a frequentist NMA using Stata 18.0to compare the efficacy of various DHIs against standard care. The quality of literature was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool (version2.0).The certainty of evidence was evaluated using the Confidence in Network Meta-Analysis (CINeMA) framework, and interventions were ranked utilizing the surface under the cumulative ranking (SUCRA)curve. A total of 44RCTs involving 8,495 patients were enrolled. The NMA revealed that for improving QoL, telephone follow-up (standardized mean difference 2.98, 95%CI 1.75-4.20) and social media (SMD 1.13, 95%CI 0.42-1.84) were statistically superior to usual care. Notably, telephone follow-up, with a SUCRA of 99.5%, appeared to be the most effective option. Regarding psychological outcomes, web-based platforms demonstrated the highest probability of being the best intervention for reducing both anxiety (SMD -1.56,95%CI-2.34 to -0.79;SUCRA 98.6%) and depression (SMD-1.07,95%CI-1.94to-0.20;SUCRA 91.4%).Safety analyses showed interactive modalities significantly reduced adverse events, whereas one-way SMS carried a significantly higher risk than interactive telephone support(OR 3.38,95%CI 1.13-10.13). The research suggests that telephone follow-up ranked highest among the included studies for improving short-term QoL, while web-based platforms showed a high probability of being effective for alleviating long-term anxiety and depression. However, these rankings should be interpreted cautiously, as intervention content, duration, and patient populations varied considerably across trials, and the small number of studies for certain modalities limits the robustness of direct comparisons. Social media interventions also emerged as a versatile option with benefits across all three outcomes, though their modest effect sizes warrant further optimization of engagement strategies. Passive SMS interventions present potential safety concerns, as their unidirectional nature may attenuate timely symptom recognition and delay appropriate care-seeking-a hypothesis supported by their significantly higher adverse event rates compared with interactive modalities. These results provide crucial evidence-based support for healthcare providers to tailor specific DHIs to individual patient needs. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261380157.

titre: Bibliometric analysis of racket sport-related injuries: global research landscape, hotspots, and trends.
auteurs: Liu Zongyu, Liu George, Li Chunying
revue: Frontiers in sports and active living
resume: This study aims to provide a comprehensive overview of racket sport-related injury research, focusing on research progress, collaboration networks, hotspots, and thematic evolution. Drawing on the Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, and PubMed, the analysis covers 1,837 publications from 76 countries spanning from 2000 to 2025. This study employed bibliometric methods combined with statistical analysis. Using CiteSpace 6.4.R1, VOSviewer 1.6.20, SCImago Graphica 1.0.53, and SPSS 26.0, quantitative and visual analyses were conducted on publication trends, geographical distribution, institutional distribution, country/region cooperation networks, core authors, journal distribution, keyword co-occurrences, research hotspots, the evolution of research topics, and highly cited papers. These analyses were supplemented by a correlation analysis, a chi-square goodness-of-fit test, and a cluster analysis. The global publication volume of racket sport-related injury research exhibited a two-stage growth trend (fluctuating growth and rapid growth), with a significant acceleration after 2020. Geographically, the research was primarily concentrated in Europe, North America, and East Asia, with the United States (527 articles), China (199 articles), and the United Kingdom (152 articles) ranking as the top three in terms of publication quantity. The statistical analysis revealed a significant positive correlation between national 2025 GDP per capita and publication volume (ρ = 0.538, p < 0.001, 95% CI [0.351, 0.684]). Core research institutions were dominated by sports universities, sports medicine hospitals, and orthopedic research centers, with the Mayo Clinic (USA), University of Liege (Belgium), and Harvard University (USA) as the leading institutions. The international cooperation network was relatively sparse, with merely 15.1% of publications involving cross-national collaboration. The cluster analysis classified research hotspots into 13 core clusters, which were further aggregated into the following six interconnected research domains: epidemiological characteristics and injury prevention, sport-specific injury manifestations, chronic overuse injuries, acute traumatic injuries, imaging-based injury diagnosis, and rehabilitation of sports injuries. The dynamic evolution of research trends was classified into the following three phases: epidemiological investigation and traditional treatment, biomechanical mechanisms and standardized intervention, and intelligent technology and precision prevention. The Brit J Sport Med was a core journal source in the field. There were extremely significant differences in article count across three research themes (χ 2 = 354.55, p < 0.001, Cramér's V = 0.54), with rehabilitation research differing significantly from both sport injury and injury prevention research. To move this field forward, scholars should foster transnational interdisciplinary collaboration, expand comparative research across populations and racket sports, implement standardized injury-surveillance and load-management frameworks, and develop generalizable, systematic prevention-rehabilitation systems for racket sport participants.

titre: Drug Use Patterns and Characteristics by Drug Type Among Drug Abusers: Findings From the Survey of Drug Abusers in Korea 2021.
auteurs: Chun Hae-Ryoung, Lee Na-Rae, Yim Hyeon Woo, Jeong Hyunsuk, Chon Younghoon, Lee Seung-Yup, Lee Hae Kook
resume: Although substance use disorders are increasingly recognized in the Republic of Korea (South Korea), empirical data on the prevalence and characteristics of drug use among treatment-seeking populations remain limited. This study examined the rate and temporal patterns of major psychoactive substance use-specifically sedatives/hypnotics/tranquilizers (sedatives), amphetamines, and marijuana/cannabis (cannabis)-across three timeframes and explored the associated sociodemographic and clinical factors. Data were obtained from 540 adults with a history of substance use, recruited from medical and rehabilitation institutions as part of the 2021 Survey of Drug Abusers in Korea. Sociodemographic and clinical factors-including Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, 5th edition (DSM-5)-based substance use disorder (SUD) diagnosis, self-recognition of addiction, depression, anxiety, and Addiction Severity Index (ASI) scores-were assessed. Group comparisons were conducted using χ² and t-tests. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with sedative, amphetamine, and cannabis use across past 30-day, past-year, and lifetime periods. Multiple linear regression examined associations between each substance and ASI composite domains. Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05. Among the 540 individuals with a history of substance use, the lifetime rate of use was highest for amphetamines (71.9%), followed by cannabis (52.8%) and sedatives (38.1%). Sedative use remained relatively consistent across timeframes (30-day: 21.9%; 1-year: 28.9%; lifetime: 38.1%), suggesting patterns of chronic or concurrent use. Across all three substance groups, participants exhibited poorer mental health, including elevated levels of depression, anxiety, or psychiatric severity. Amphetamine and sedative users were more likely to be female, older, and of lower socioeconomic and educational status, with greater impairment in psychiatric, family, and social functioning, as well as higher self-recognition of addiction. In contrast, cannabis users were predominantly younger males with higher socioeconomic status but elevated anxiety levels. Institutional affiliation also differed by substance type: cannabis users were more frequently associated with rehabilitation centers, whereas amphetamine users were more often treated in medical institutions. Findings highlight the coexistence of shared psychosocial vulnerabilities and substance-specific risk profiles in Korea. Integrated, multidimensional interventions-linking psychiatric care, social support, and economic protection-are needed for amphetamine and sedative users. For younger cannabis users, early intervention and relapse prevention are essential. Strengthening coordination between medical and rehabilitation systems under Korea's Judicial-Treatment-Rehabilitation Linkage Model may reduce stigma and enhance recovery-oriented care for individuals with SUD.

titre: Continuity of care interventions for people with stroke and their caregivers: a scoping review of randomized controlled trials.
auteurs: Premnazeer Meera, Munce Sarah E P, Bayley Mark T, Seto Ellen, Wong Natalie, Kokorelias Kristina M, Gill Monique, Scali Orianna L, Sessford James, Cameron Jill I
resume: People with stroke (PwS) and their family caregivers characterize transitions across care environments as challenging. Enhancing the family-centered nature of continuity of care interventions could improve experiences and outcomes. This scoping review aimed to synthesize the literature on continuity of care interventions for PwS and/or their caregivers. The Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology for scoping reviews was followed. Five databases were searched, and only randomized controlled trials were included. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and deductive content analysis. We included 65 interventions identified from 80 included studies. Most intervention studies included only PwS. Most interventions addressed the transition from acute inpatient management to home care services. On average, two of three continuity of care dimensions were addressed, and two of four family-centred care components were addressed across interventions. This scoping review emphasizes the need for continuity of care intervention studies to include both PwS and their caregivers. Future research should investigate interventions that promote a family-centered care approach. The review also highlights that current interventions do not address all transitions across the stroke care continuum. Finally, future interventions should explore which aspects of continuity of care may need to be prioritized at specific transition points.

titre: Refining Home-Based Squat Training: The Role of Hip Adduction in Improving Neuromuscular Control for Clinically Diagnosed Patellofemoral Pain Syndrome.
auteurs: Chen Chia-Ling, Lo Sui-Foon, Chiu Min-Chi, Chang Chien-Chun, Hong Wei-Hsien
revue: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
resume: BACKGROUND Patellofemoral pain syndrome (PFPS) often stems from neuromuscular imbalances, particularly vastus medialis obliques (VMO) dysfunction impairing patellar tracking. Research is shifting toward integrated rehabilitation strategies, such as combining hip adduction with squats to enhance VMO recruitment. MATERIAL AND METHODS Thirty participants with PFPS were randomized to traditional squatting (SQU, n=15) or squatting with hip adduction (SQU-HA, n=15) for an 8-week home-based program with identical stretching. SQU-HA squeezed a Swiss ball during squats. Fifteen healthy individuals served as a reference group (RG). Outcome measures assessed before and after intervention included Q-angle, patellar tilt, clinical scales (visual analog scale [VAS], patellofemoral pain severity scale [PSS]), and electromyographic parameters (VMO, vastus lateralis [VL], adductor [ADD] amplitudes, onset times, VMO/VL ratio, and VMO-VL onset difference). RESULTS Both PFPS groups showed significant improvements in VAS and PSS after intervention, with greater VAS improvement in the SQU-HA group (P<0.01). Within-group analysis showed reduced patellar tilt in the SQU-HA group (P=0.003); between-group comparison did not reach statistical significance (P=0.217). Muscle activation onset sequences shifted from an abnormal pattern, in which VL activation preceded VMO and ADD activation, to a more typical pattern, in which VMO activation preceded VL and ADD activation. This shift was particularly evident in the SQU-HA group, whose activation pattern resembled that of the RG after intervention. Only VMO-VL onset difference, VMO/VL ratio, and Q-angle were correlated with clinical outcomes (P<0.05). CONCLUSIONS An 8-week SQU-HA program demonstrates promising short-term improvements in VMO-related neuromuscular measures and pain reduction for patients with PFPS. This accessible motor re-education strategy serves as a practical, home-based approach to patellofemoral rehabilitation.

titre: Perioperative nutrition therapy in high-risk patients: A narrative review.
auteurs: Wobith Maria, Strobel Rahel, Klek Stanislaw, Ljungqvist Olle, Wischmeyer Paul, Weimann Arved
revue: Nutrition in clinical practice : official publication of the American Society for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition
resume: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS), as the plan A and standard for perioperative management, has shifted the focus from routine nutritional support toward the early identification and targeted management of high-risk patients. The new ICD-11 code for undernutrition offers an opportunity to better identify and characterize surgical patients at nutritional risk, while also potentially improving clinical recognition, acceptance of nutritional risk as a relevant perioperative condition, and reimbursement for targeted nutritional interventions. Early preoperative interventions should be considered. While short-term nutritional conditioning over 10-14 days primarily aims to correct nutritional and metabolic deficits, multimodal prehabilitation ideally requires 3-6 weeks to achieve meaningful improvements in physical fitness, functional capacity, and physiological reserve, particularly in patients undergoing major surgery after neoadjuvant therapy. Perioperative targeted strategies include carbohydrate loading (CHO drinks), immunomodulation, omega-3-fatty acids, hydroxymethylbutyrate, and probiotics or synbiotics. While parenteral nutrition is generally not required in low-risk patients with an uncomplicated recovery, the indication for supplemental (peripheral) parenteral nutrition should not be missed in high-risk patients with inadequate oral or enteral intake. Structured postoperative, post-discharge nutritional monitoring and rehabilitation should be integrated more consistently, especially in patients with eventful and complicated clinical courses.

titre: [ZHUANG Lixing's experience of mind-regulating and pivot-restoring therapy in treatment of postural instability of Parkinson's disease].
auteurs: Liao Kaihao, Fan Jingqi, Liu Xin, Han Mingda, Zhuang Lixing
revue: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
resume: This paper summarizes Professor ZHUANG Lixing's clinical experience in treatment of postural instability in Parkinson's disease (PD) with acupuncture. The core pathogenesis of this disease lies in "imbalanced pivoting" of the governor vessel, Shaoyang meridians and the belt vessel. The pathological evolution follows the pattern of "loss of spirit/mind governance, loss of qi pivoting, and loss of physical function". The therapeutic principle is "mind-regulating, pivot-restoring, and sinew-relaxing", with the method of "mind-regulating and pivot-restoring" operated throughout treatment. The main acupoint prescriptions include "mind-regulating needling" (Sishenzhen, Shenting [GV24], Yintang [GV24+], Shenmen [HT7] Sanyinjiao [SP6]), "pivot-restoring acupoints" (Dusanzhen, Fengchi [GB20], Waiguan [TE5], Zulinqi [GB41]), and "the sinew-relaxing acupoints" (Yanglingquan [GB34], Luansanzhen, aishi point). Treatment is administered according to the stage of disease progression and the acupoints are modified based on symptoms, and the acupuncture technique of "directing qi to preserve essence", and fire needling are combined. This therapeutic idea emphasizes the integration of acupuncture and rehabilitation training, adopts staging treatment based on illness conditions, and demonstrates clear therapeutic effect. This therapeutic regimen can stabilize the central axis, correct gait, relieve contracture, improve motor function and enhance quality of life in PD patients with postural instability.

titre: Exploring relational and humanizing processes in a structured shelter dog programme: A qualitative study in psychiatric rehabilitation.
auteurs: Díaz María José Ferreira
resume: Long-stay psychiatric rehabilitation units often struggle to provide emotionally meaningful and person-centred care because of institutional routines and limited opportunities for therapeutic engagement. Innovative relational interventions may help promote emotional connection and support more humanized models of psychiatric rehabilitation. To explore the emotional and relational processes observed during a structured shelter dog programme in a long-stay psychiatric rehabilitation setting and to examine how these processes were perceived to contribute to the humanization of care. A descriptive qualitative study was conducted using participant observation across eight intervention sessions, one focus group with healthcare professionals, and one semi-structured interview with the dog handler. Data were analysed using Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis framework. Three themes emerged: (1) Emotional reawakening, describing renewed emotional expression and positive affect; (2) The dog as a relational bridge, illustrating how the dogs facilitated interpersonal communication and therapeutic engagement; and (3) Shared humanity and relational care, reflecting enhanced relational awareness, professional reflection, and a more person-centred experience of care. Participants perceived the shelter dog programme as a meaningful relational intervention that promoted emotional engagement, interpersonal connection, and more humanized psychiatric care. These findings suggest that structured relational interventions involving carefully selected shelter dogs may complement recovery-oriented psychiatric rehabilitation. Further research should explore patient perspectives, longer-term outcomes, and implementation across different mental health settings.
